manifest.title: QPTAS for Max Weight Independent Set in Graphs with Strongly Edge-Sublinear Separators

inputs.abstract:
A hereditary graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if its
$m$-edge graphs admit balanced separators of size $O(m^b)$ for some
$0\le b<1$. Maximum-weight independent set admits a deterministic
quasipolynomial-time approximation scheme on every such class.
Given rational vertex weights and rational $0<\varepsilon<1$, the scheme
returns an independent set of weight at least $(1-\varepsilon)$ times
the optimum in time
$\exp((\varepsilon^{-1}\log(n+2))^{O(1)})+(\ell+1)^{O(1)}$,
where $\ell$ is the binary encoding length of the weights and accuracy
and the constants depend only on the class. No separator is required
as part of the input.

concepts.title: Explicit integer budgets for the round-or-cut algorithm
concepts.description:
Fixed class constants and an integer accuracy denominator determine the
load, edge sparsity, conditioning level, and small-target cutoff.
The conditioning moment floor supplies a uniform protected radius.
A larger integer precision budget makes that dyadic radius small enough
using only natural arithmetic and powers of two.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The precision budget is the protected-radius denominator plus two.
That denominator is quasipolynomial in the input order and accuracy, so
this conservative choice also gives a quasipolynomial iteration budget.
The proof of the main theorem combines these budgets with the resource
estimates and concrete RAM execution.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.MomentLP
import Lax263307.HeavyConditioning
import Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log

/-!
---
title: Explicit integer budgets for the round-or-cut algorithm
type: lemma
---
Fixed class constants and an integer accuracy denominator determine the
load, edge sparsity, conditioning level, and small-target cutoff.
The conditioning moment floor supplies a uniform protected radius.
A larger integer precision budget makes that dyadic radius small enough
using only natural arithmetic and powers of two.

# Formalization notes

The precision budget is the protected-radius denominator plus two.
That denominator is quasipolynomial in the input order and accuracy, so
this conservative choice also gives a quasipolynomial iteration budget.
The proof of the main theorem combines these budgets with the resource
estimates and concrete RAM execution.
-/

namespace Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters

open HeavyConditioning (probabilityFloor)
open MomentLP (dimension)
open RoundedOracleSearch (steps)
def logarithm (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.log2 (2 * n) + 1
def load (B n D : ℕ) : ℕ := 12 * B * D * logarithm n
def targetThreshold (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ := K * (load B n D + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2)
def sparsity (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 * targetThreshold a K B n D
def level (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ := sparsity a K B n D * (Nat.log2 n + 1)
def cutoff (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ := max (targetThreshold a K B n D) (level a K B n D)
def floorDenominator (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  2 * n * sparsity a K B n D * (Nat.log2 n + 1)
def momentFloor (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  1 / (floorDenominator a K B n D : ℚ) ^ level a K B n D
def radiusDenominator (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  256 * dimension n (level a K B n D) * n ^ 2 * D ^ 2 *
    floorDenominator a K B n D ^ level a K B n D
def precision (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ := radiusDenominator a K B n D + 2
def iterations (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  steps (dimension n (level a K B n D)) (precision a K B n D)

axiom budgets {a K B n D k : ℕ} (hK : 0 < K) (hB : 0 < B)
    (hD : 4 ≤ D) (large : cutoff a K B n D < k) :
    0 < load B n D ∧ 0 < sparsity a K B n D ∧ 0 < level a K B n D ∧
      0 < (1 / (D : ℝ)) ∧ (1 / (D : ℝ)) ≤ 1 / 4 ∧
      12 * (B : ℝ) * ((Nat.log2 (2 * n) : ℝ) + 1) ≤
        (1 / (D : ℝ)) * load B n D ∧
      (sparsity a K B n D : ℝ) * ((Nat.log2 n : ℝ) + 1) ≤ level a K B n D ∧
      (K : ℝ) * ((load B n D : ℝ) + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2) ≤ k ∧
      (2 * K : ℝ) * ((load B n D : ℝ) + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2) ≤ sparsity a K B n D

axiom conditioning_floor (a K B n D : ℕ) :
    (momentFloor a K B n D : ℝ) =
      probabilityFloor n (sparsity a K B n D) ^ level a K B n D

axiom protected_radius {a K B n D : ℕ} (hK : 0 < K) (hn : 0 < n) (hD : 0 < D) :
    2 ≤ precision a K B n D ∧
      ((2 : ℝ) ^ precision a K B n D)⁻¹ ≤
        (momentFloor a K B n D : ℝ) /
          (256 * (dimension n (level a K B n D) : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * (D : ℝ) ^ 2)

end Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters

statements.signature: budgets : failed to pretty print expression (use 'set_option pp.rawOnError true' for raw representation)

conditioning_floor : ∀ (a K B n D : Nat),
  Eq (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.momentFloor a K B n D).cast
    (instHPow.hPow (Lax263307.HeavyConditioning.probabilityFloor n (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.sparsity a K B n D))
      (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.level a K B n D))

protected_radius : ∀ {a K B n D : Nat},
  instLTNat.lt 0 K →
    instLTNat.lt 0 n →
      instLTNat.lt 0 D →
        And (instLENat.le 2 (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.precision a K B n D))
          (Real.instLE.le (Real.instInv.inv (instHPow.hPow 2 (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.precision a K B n D)))
            (instHDiv.hDiv (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.momentFloor a K B n D).cast
              (instHMul.hMul
                (instHMul.hMul
                  (instHMul.hMul 256
                    (Lax263307.MomentLP.dimension n (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.level a K B n D)).cast)
                  (instHPow.hPow n.cast 2))
                (instHPow.hPow D.cast 2))))

concepts.title: Treewidth transfer through an almost-embedding
concepts.description:
An almost-embedding maps each vertex of $H$ into $G$ and assigns to each edge
a connected vertex set joining its mapped endpoints. Sets assigned to
nonincident edges are disjoint. If $H$ has maximum degree at most $d$ and
no isolated vertices, a decomposition of $G$ with bags of size at most $w$
gives a decomposition of $H$ with bags of size at most $2dw$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The connected vertex sets can in particular be the supports of the simple
paths in the paper. This slightly more general definition keeps precisely
the properties needed for tree-decomposition transfer. Mapped vertices need
not be distinct, and singleton routes are allowed. An induced almost-embedding
also forbids edges between routes assigned to nonincident edges.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.ConnectedRepresentations
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite

/-!
---
title: Treewidth transfer through an almost-embedding
type: lemma
---
An almost-embedding maps each vertex of $H$ into $G$ and assigns to each edge
a connected vertex set joining its mapped endpoints. Sets assigned to
nonincident edges are disjoint. If $H$ has maximum degree at most $d$ and
no isolated vertices, a decomposition of $G$ with bags of size at most $w$
gives a decomposition of $H$ with bags of size at most $2dw$.

# Formalization notes

The connected vertex sets can in particular be the supports of the simple
paths in the paper. This slightly more general definition keeps precisely
the properties needed for tree-decomposition transfer. Mapped vertices need
not be distinct, and singleton routes are allowed. An induced almost-embedding
also forbids edges between routes assigned to nonincident edges.
-/

namespace Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings

open Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- A connected route for every edge, disjoint for nonincident edges. -/
structure AlmostEmbedding {t n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t))
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) where
  /-- Vertex images, with no injectivity requirement. -/
  vertexMap : Fin t → Fin n
  /-- Host vertices on each route. -/
  route : H.edgeSet → Finset (Fin n)
  /-- Each route is nonempty and connected. -/
  connected : ∀ e, (G.induce (↑(route e) : Set (Fin n))).Connected
  /-- A route contains the images of its edge's endpoints. -/
  endpoints : ∀ e v, v ∈ e.val → vertexMap v ∈ route e
  /-- Routes of nonincident edges share no host vertex. -/
  disjoint : ∀ e f, Disjoint e.val.toFinset f.val.toFinset → Disjoint (route e) (route f)

/-- In addition, nonincident routes have no edges between them in the host. -/
def IsInduced {t n : ℕ} {H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) : Prop :=
  ∀ e f, Disjoint e.val.toFinset f.val.toFinset →
    ∀ a ∈ E.route e, ∀ b ∈ E.route f, ¬G.Adj a b

/-- The union of all routes incident to one represented vertex. -/
noncomputable def vertexCarrier {t n : ℕ} {H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)}
    {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)} (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) (v : Fin t) : Finset (Fin n) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.biUnion fun e : H.edgeSet => if v ∈ e.val then E.route e else ∅

/-- An almost-embedding transfers decompositions with at most factor `2d` loss. -/
axiom transfer_decomposition {t n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t))
    [DecidableRel H.Adj] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (E : AlmostEmbedding H G)
    (d w : ℕ) (degree_bound : ∀ v, H.degree v ≤ d)
    (no_isolates : ∀ v, ¬H.IsIsolated v)
    (D : TreeDecomposition G) (bag_bound : ∀ i, (D.bag i).card ≤ w) :
    ∃ D' : TreeDecomposition H, ∀ i, (D'.bag i).card ≤ 2 * d * w

end Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings

statements.signature:
transfer_decomposition : ∀ {t n : Nat} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [inst : DecidableRel H.Adj] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
  (E : Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings.AlmostEmbedding H G) (d w : Nat),
  (∀ (v : Fin t), instLENat.le (H.degree v) d) →
    (∀ (v : Fin t), Not (H.IsIsolated v)) →
      ∀ (D : Lax228581.Treewidth.TreeDecomposition G),
        (∀ (i : D.Node), instLENat.le (D.bag i).card w) →
          Exists fun D' => ∀ (i : D'.Node), instLENat.le (D'.bag i).card (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 2 d) w)
statements.doc: An almost-embedding transfers decompositions with at most factor `2d` loss.

concepts.title: Balanced closed parts certify a balanced separator
concepts.description:
A partition of undeleted vertices into parts closed under undeleted graph
edges places each connected component wholly inside one part. If every
part has at most two thirds of the original vertices, the deleted set is
a balanced separator. This permits the parts supplied by repeated cuts.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.SeparatorComponents
import Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators

/-!
---
title: Balanced closed parts certify a balanced separator
type: lemma
---
A partition of undeleted vertices into parts closed under undeleted graph
edges places each connected component wholly inside one part. If every
part has at most two thirds of the original vertices, the deleted set is
a balanced separator. This permits the parts supplied by repeated cuts.
-/

namespace Lax263307.BalancedPartitions

open SeparatorComponents EdgeSublinearSeparators

axiom balanced_separator {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n))
    {ι : Type} (P : Partition G S ι) (balanced : ∀ i, 3 * (P.vertices i).card ≤ 2 * n) :
    IsBalancedSeparator G S

end Lax263307.BalancedPartitions

statements.signature:
balanced_separator : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) {ι : Type}
  (P : Lax263307.SeparatorComponents.Partition G S ι),
  (∀ (i : ι), instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul 3 (P.vertices i).card) (instHMul.hMul 2 n)) →
    Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators.IsBalancedSeparator G S

concepts.title: Sublinear bag bounds survive independent blow-ups
concepts.description:
The independent blow-up closure of a hereditary class with strongly
edge-sublinear separators also has edge-sublinear decomposition bags.
Restrict the original host to vertices used by the projection. Choosing
one representative in each fibre embeds this host into the blow-up, so
its edge count cannot exceed that of the blow-up. Optimize degree deletion
and bounded-fibre lifting, then convert the resulting real exponent to
an integer power bound.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Arbitrary projection fibres, including empty fibres, are allowed. Relabel
used host vertices and enumerate each fibre to identify the graph with an
explicit copy graph. The original host need not have at most as many edges
until its unused vertices are removed. These existential constructions
are structural analysis; the algorithm does not build decomposition bags.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.EdgeBagBounds
import Lax263307.BlowUpClasses
import Lax263307.BlowUpDeletion

/-!
---
title: Sublinear bag bounds survive independent blow-ups
type: lemma
---
The independent blow-up closure of a hereditary class with strongly
edge-sublinear separators also has edge-sublinear decomposition bags.
Restrict the original host to vertices used by the projection. Choosing
one representative in each fibre embeds this host into the blow-up, so
its edge count cannot exceed that of the blow-up. Optimize degree deletion
and bounded-fibre lifting, then convert the resulting real exponent to
an integer power bound.

# Formalization notes

Arbitrary projection fibres, including empty fibres, are allowed. Relabel
used host vertices and enumerate each fibre to identify the graph with an
explicit copy graph. The original host need not have at most as many edges
until its unused vertices are removed. These existential constructions
are structural analysis; the algorithm does not build decomposition bags.
-/

namespace Lax263307.BlowUpBagBounds

open PowerBagBounds (HasPowerBagBound)
open GraphClasses EdgeSublinearSeparators BlowUpClasses Lax228581.Treewidth

axiom blowup_sublinear_bag_bound (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (separators : HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C) :
    ∃ β c : ℝ, 0 ≤ β ∧ β < 1 ∧ 0 < c ∧ ∀ m (H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)), H ∈ blowUpClass C m →
      ∃ D : TreeDecomposition H, ∀ j,
        ((D.bag j).card : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.rpow ((H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) + 1) β

axiom blowup_power_bag_bound (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (separators : HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C) :
    ∃ a A : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ 0 < A ∧ HasPowerBagBound (blowUpClass C) a A

end Lax263307.BlowUpBagBounds

statements.signature:
blowup_power_bag_bound : ∀ (C : Lax263307.GraphClasses.GraphClass),
  Lax263307.GraphClasses.IsHereditary C →
    Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators.HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C →
      Exists fun a =>
        Exists fun A =>
          And (instLTNat.lt 0 a)
            (And (instLTNat.lt 0 A)
              (Lax263307.PowerBagBounds.HasPowerBagBound (Lax263307.BlowUpClasses.blowUpClass C) a A))

blowup_sublinear_bag_bound : ∀ (C : Lax263307.GraphClasses.GraphClass),
  Lax263307.GraphClasses.IsHereditary C →
    Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators.HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C →
      Exists fun β =>
        Exists fun c =>
          And (Real.instLE.le 0 β)
            (And (Real.instLT.lt β 1)
              (And (Real.instLT.lt 0 c)
                (∀ (m : Nat) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)),
                  Set.instMembership.mem (Lax263307.BlowUpClasses.blowUpClass C m) H →
                    Exists fun D =>
                      ∀ (j : D.Node),
                        Real.instLE.le (D.bag j).card.cast
                          (instHMul.hMul c ((instHAdd.hAdd H.edgeSet.ncard.cast 1).rpow β)))))

concepts.title: Independent blow-up classes are hereditary
concepts.description:
The independent blow-up closure of a graph class consists of finite graphs
whose vertices project to a member of that class, with adjacency exactly
determined by adjacency of the projected vertices. This closure is hereditary.
The explicitly constructed copy graphs belong to it after relabeling.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Projection fibres are independent, and between two fibres all edges or no
edges are present. Empty fibres are allowed, matching the zero multiplicities
in the weighted reduction. With this convention the closure is hereditary
for every original class. For a hereditary original class it agrees with
the paper's convention of nonempty fibres: delete the unused host vertices
before constructing the blow-up.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.GraphClasses
import Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp

/-!
---
title: Independent blow-up classes are hereditary
type: lemma
---
The independent blow-up closure of a graph class consists of finite graphs
whose vertices project to a member of that class, with adjacency exactly
determined by adjacency of the projected vertices. This closure is hereditary.
The explicitly constructed copy graphs belong to it after relabeling.

# Formalization notes

Projection fibres are independent, and between two fibres all edges or no
edges are present. Empty fibres are allowed, matching the zero multiplicities
in the weighted reduction. With this convention the closure is hereditary
for every original class. For a hereditary original class it agrees with
the paper's convention of nonempty fibres: delete the unused host vertices
before constructing the blow-up.
-/

namespace Lax263307.BlowUpClasses

open GraphClasses IndependentBlowUp

/-- Graphs obtained by independent blow-ups of members, allowing empty fibres. -/
def blowUpClass (C : GraphClass) : GraphClass :=
  fun m => {H | ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ C n ∧
    ∃ projection : Fin m → Fin n,
      ∀ u v, H.Adj u v ↔ G.Adj (projection u) (projection v)}

/-- Restricting an independent blow-up to any induced subgraph remains a blow-up. -/
axiom hereditary_closure (C : GraphClass) : IsHereditary (blowUpClass C)

/-- Relabeling the explicit copy graph places it in the blow-up closure. -/
axiom copy_graph_mem (C : GraphClass) {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (member : G ∈ C n) (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (m : ℕ) (labeling : Fin m ≃ Vertex copies) :
    (graph G copies).comap labeling ∈ blowUpClass C m

end Lax263307.BlowUpClasses

  Set.instMembership.mem (C n) G →
    ∀ (copies : Fin n → Nat) (m : Nat) (labeling : Equiv (Fin m) (Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp.Vertex copies)),
      Set.instMembership.mem (Lax263307.BlowUpClasses.blowUpClass C m)
        (SimpleGraph.comap (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe labeling) (Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp.graph G copies))

concepts.title: Lifting a tree decomposition through a bounded blow-up
concepts.description:
Suppose $G$ has treewidth at most $w$, and every vertex is replaced by at
most $s$ independent copies. The blow-up has a tree decomposition whose
bags have size at most $s(w+1)$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The original decomposition tree is retained, and each vertex in a bag is
replaced by all its copies. An empty fibre contributes no vertices.
The conclusion is expressed directly as a bag-size bound using the
registered `Lax228581.Treewidth.TreeDecomposition` definition.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.BlowUpIndependentSets
import Lax228581.Treewidth

/-!
---
title: Lifting a tree decomposition through a bounded blow-up
type: lemma
---
Suppose $G$ has treewidth at most $w$, and every vertex is replaced by at
most $s$ independent copies. The blow-up has a tree decomposition whose
bags have size at most $s(w+1)$.

# Formalization notes

The original decomposition tree is retained, and each vertex in a bag is
replaced by all its copies. An empty fibre contributes no vertices.
The conclusion is expressed directly as a bag-size bound using the
registered `Lax228581.Treewidth.TreeDecomposition` definition.
-/

namespace Lax263307.BlowUpDecompositions

open IndependentBlowUp Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- Replacing every bag vertex by its copies multiplies bag sizes by at most `s`. -/
axiom bounded_blowup_decomposition {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (s w : ℕ) (bounded : ∀ v, copies v ≤ s)
    (width : HasTreewidthAtMost G w) :
    ∃ D : TreeDecomposition (graph G copies), ∀ i, (D.bag i).card ≤ s * (w + 1)

end Lax263307.BlowUpDecompositions

statements.signature:
bounded_blowup_decomposition : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (copies : Fin n → Nat) (s w : Nat),
  (∀ (v : Fin n), instLENat.le (copies v) s) →
    Lax228581.Treewidth.HasTreewidthAtMost G w →
      Exists fun D => ∀ (i : D.Node), instLENat.le (D.bag i).card (instHMul.hMul s (instHAdd.hAdd w 1))
statements.doc: Replacing every bag vertex by its copies multiplies bag sizes by at most `s`.

concepts.title: Deleting high-degree vertices in an independent blow-up
concepts.description:
Let $H$ be an independent blow-up of a graph of treewidth at most $w$.
Delete the vertices $X$ whose degree exceeds an integer threshold $s$.
Then $s|X|\le 2|E(H)|$, and $H$ has a tree decomposition with bags of size
at most
$$|X|+\max\{1,s(w+1)\}.$$

Large fibres become isolated after this deletion. The remaining nonisolated
vertices therefore embed into a blow-up with at most $s$ copies per vertex.
The maximum with one covers singleton bags for isolated vertices, including
the edgeless case and threshold zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.BlowUpDecompositions
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.DegreeSum
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

/-!
---
title: Deleting high-degree vertices in an independent blow-up
type: lemma
---
Let $H$ be an independent blow-up of a graph of treewidth at most $w$.
Delete the vertices $X$ whose degree exceeds an integer threshold $s$.
Then $s|X|\le 2|E(H)|$, and $H$ has a tree decomposition with bags of size
at most
$$|X|+\max\{1,s(w+1)\}.$$

Large fibres become isolated after this deletion. The remaining nonisolated
vertices therefore embed into a blow-up with at most $s$ copies per vertex.
The maximum with one covers singleton bags for isolated vertices, including
the edgeless case and threshold zero.
-/

namespace Lax263307.BlowUpDeletion

open IndependentBlowUp Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- The vertices removed at degree threshold `s`. -/
noncomputable def highDegree {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (s : ℕ) : Finset (Vertex copies) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter fun v => s < (graph G copies).degree v

/-- The degree sum bounds the number of removed vertices. -/
axiom high_degree_card {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (s : ℕ) :
    s * (highDegree G copies s).card ≤ 2 * (graph G copies).edgeSet.ncard

/-- Lift bounded fibres, add singleton bags, and restore the deleted set. -/
axiom deletion_decomposition {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (s w : ℕ) (width : HasTreewidthAtMost G w) :
    ∃ D : TreeDecomposition (graph G copies),
      ∀ i, (D.bag i).card ≤ (highDegree G copies s).card + max 1 (s * (w + 1))

/-- Choosing the degree threshold balances the two terms of the estimate. -/
axiom power_bound {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (w : ℕ) (b c : ℝ) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hb₁ : b < 1)
    (hc : 0 < c) (width : HasTreewidthAtMost G w)
    (width_bound : (w + 1 : ℕ) ≤
      c * Real.rpow ((graph G copies).edgeSet.ncard + 1) b) :
    ∃ D : TreeDecomposition (graph G copies), ∀ i,
      ((D.bag i).card : ℝ) ≤ (3 + 2 * c) *
        Real.rpow ((graph G copies).edgeSet.ncard + 1) ((1 + b) / 2)

end Lax263307.BlowUpDeletion

statements.signature:
deletion_decomposition : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (copies : Fin n → Nat) (s w : Nat),
  Lax228581.Treewidth.HasTreewidthAtMost G w →
    Exists fun D =>
      ∀ (i : D.Node),
        instLENat.le (D.bag i).card
          (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax263307.BlowUpDeletion.highDegree G copies s).card
            (Nat.instMax.max 1 (instHMul.hMul s (instHAdd.hAdd w 1))))
statements.doc: Lift bounded fibres, add singleton bags, and restore the deleted set.

statements.signature:
high_degree_card : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (copies : Fin n → Nat) (s : Nat),
  instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul s (Lax263307.BlowUpDeletion.highDegree G copies s).card)
    (instHMul.hMul 2 (Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp.graph G copies).edgeSet.ncard)
statements.doc: The degree sum bounds the number of removed vertices.

statements.signature:
power_bound : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (copies : Fin n → Nat) (w : Nat) (b c : Real),
  Real.instLE.le 0 b →
    Real.instLT.lt b 1 →
      Real.instLT.lt 0 c →
        Lax228581.Treewidth.HasTreewidthAtMost G w →
          Real.instLE.le (instHAdd.hAdd w 1).cast
              (instHMul.hMul c

concepts.title: Independent sets lift and project through a blow-up
concepts.description:
An independent set of the original graph lifts to an independent set
containing all its copies. An independent set of copies projects to an
independent set of the original graph. The lift of $I$ has size
$\sum_{v\in I}t_v$, and every set of copies $K$ satisfies
$|K|\le\sum_{v\in\operatorname{project}(K)}t_v$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp

/-!
---
title: Independent sets lift and project through a blow-up
type: lemma
---
An independent set of the original graph lifts to an independent set
containing all its copies. An independent set of copies projects to an
independent set of the original graph. The lift of $I$ has size
$\sum_{v\in I}t_v$, and every set of copies $K$ satisfies
$|K|\le\sum_{v\in\operatorname{project}(K)}t_v$.
-/

namespace Lax263307.BlowUpIndependentSets

open IndependentBlowUp

/-- Taking all copies preserves independence. -/
axiom lift_independent {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (copies : Fin n → ℕ)
    (I : Finset (Fin n)) (independent : G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n))) :
    (graph G copies).IsIndepSet (lift copies I : Set (Vertex copies))

/-- Projecting any independent set of copies preserves independence. -/
axiom project_independent {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (copies : Fin n → ℕ)
    (K : Finset (Vertex copies)) (independent : (graph G copies).IsIndepSet (K : Set (Vertex copies))) :
    G.IsIndepSet (project K : Set (Fin n))

/-- The lift contains exactly the sum of the selected vertices' multiplicities. -/
axiom lift_cardinality {n : ℕ} (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (I : Finset (Fin n)) :
    (lift copies I).card = ∑ v ∈ I, copies v

/-- A set of copies is contained in the complete lift of its projection. -/
axiom projection_capacity {n : ℕ} (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (K : Finset (Vertex copies)) :
    K.card ≤ ∑ v ∈ project K, copies v

end Lax263307.BlowUpIndependentSets

concepts.title: Protected balls for the rounded ellipsoid method
concepts.description:
Scaling a moment vector in the unit cube by 4N puts it well inside the
initial unit ball. A perturbation of Euclidean radius at most one quarter
stays in that ball. Euclidean balls are contained in the corresponding
coordinate cubes, so the central-cut buffers apply to them. Every nonzero
integer normal has squared Euclidean norm at least one.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The squared norms use finite dot products, matching the registered LP
ellipsoid sequence. These geometric estimates do not assume that the
independent-set hull has interior. Coordinate scaling is defined over an
arbitrary field so its rational specialization is computable.

concepts.title: Integer coefficients of recursive separating cuts
concepts.description:
The cut for a part $C$ and bound $u$ is
$$\sum_{v\in C}z_{A\cup\{v\}}-u z_A\le0.$$
Collect repeated coordinates into an integer coefficient vector. Evaluating
that vector gives exactly the left-hand side of the component inequality.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.ComponentCuts
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Powerset

/-!
---
title: Integer coefficients of recursive separating cuts
type: lemma
---
The cut for a part $C$ and bound $u$ is
$$\sum_{v\in C}z_{A\cup\{v\}}-u z_A\le0.$$
Collect repeated coordinates into an integer coefficient vector. Evaluating
that vector gives exactly the left-hand side of the component inequality.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding

open LinearRelaxation

/-- The coefficient at one coordinate, after collecting all repeated terms. -/
def coefficient {n r : ℕ} (A C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ)
    (B : Coordinate n r) : ℤ :=
  (∑ v ∈ C, if insert v A = B.val then 1 else 0) -
    if A = B.val then (u : ℤ) else 0

/-- Evaluate the coefficient vector in the real coordinate space. -/
noncomputable def evaluate {n r : ℕ} (a : Coordinate n r → ℤ)
    (z : MomentVector n r) : ℝ := ∑ B, (a B : ℝ) * z B

/-- The collected coefficient vector represents exactly the intended cut. -/
axiom evaluation_identity {n r : ℕ} (A C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ)
    (size : A.card ≤ r) (z : MomentVector n r) :
    evaluate (coefficient A C u) z =
      (∑ v ∈ C, value z (insert v A)) - (u : ℝ) * value z A

end Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding

  instLENat.le A.card r →
    ∀ (z : Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.MomentVector n r),
      Eq (Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding.evaluate (Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding.coefficient A C u) z)
        (instHSub.hSub (C.sum fun v => Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.value z (Finset.instInsert.insert v A))
          (instHMul.hMul u.cast (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.value z A)))

concepts.title: Valid separating inequalities from independent-set bounds
concepts.description:
Suppose every independent set in $G[C]$ has size at most $u$.
For $|A|\le r$, every $z\in P_r(G,k)$ satisfies
$$\sum_{v\in C}z_{A\cup\{v\}}\le u z_A.$$

The set $C$ need not be a connected component;
the algorithm applies this statement to the components left by a separator.

import Lax263307.LinearRelaxation

/-!
---
title: Valid separating inequalities from independent-set bounds
type: lemma
---
Suppose every independent set in $G[C]$ has size at most $u$.
For $|A|\le r$, every $z\in P_r(G,k)$ satisfies
$$\sum_{v\in C}z_{A\cup\{v\}}\le u z_A.$$

The set $C$ need not be a connected component;
the algorithm applies this statement to the components left by a separator.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ComponentCuts

open LinearRelaxation

/-- A certified independence bound supplies an inequality valid on the exact hull. -/
axiom valid_cut {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k r : ℕ)
    (C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ) (bound : IsIndependenceBound G C u)
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (size : A.card ≤ r)
    (z : MomentVector n r) (member : z ∈ independentSetHull G k r) :
    ∑ v ∈ C, value z (insert v A) ≤ (u : ℝ) * value z A

end Lax263307.ComponentCuts

concepts.title: Computing the recursive answer-or-cut decision
concepts.description:
Round each part's rational cost to a target. Skip queries on light parts.
Scan child answers in a fixed order: the first failed query determines the
returned component inequality; if all required queries succeed, return the
union of their independent sets. The selected inequality has the required
positive gap and coefficient bound, and the returned union has the required
approximation guarantee.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The decision and target formulas are computable. Child-query correctness is
an explicit induction hypothesis for this one recursive step. This does not
assert correctness or a RAM bound for the complete recursive program.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.HeavyRecursiveRounding
import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Floor

/-!
---
title: Computing the recursive answer-or-cut decision
type: lemma
---
Round each part's rational cost to a target. Skip queries on light parts.
Scan child answers in a fixed order: the first failed query determines the
returned component inequality; if all required queries succeed, return the
union of their independent sets. The selected inequality has the required
positive gap and coefficient bound, and the returned union has the required
approximation guarantee.

# Formalization notes

The decision and target formulas are computable. Child-query correctness is
an explicit induction hypothesis for this one recursive step. This does not
assert correctness or a RAM bound for the complete recursive program.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ComputedRounding

open SeparatorComponents (combine)

def target (δ cost : ℚ) : ℕ := ⌊(1 - δ) * cost⌋₊ + 1

def answer {n : ℕ} {ι : Type} (δ : ℚ) (k : ℕ) (cost : ι → ℚ)
    (query : ι → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))) (i : ι) : Option (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  if δ * k / (4 * n) < cost i then query i (target δ (cost i)) else some ∅

inductive Result (n : ℕ)
  | found (vertices : Finset (Fin n))
  | cut (vertices : Finset (Fin n)) (bound : ℕ)

def collect {n : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (order : List ι) (parts : ι → Finset (Fin n))
    (δ : ℚ) (k : ℕ) (cost : ι → ℚ) (query : ι → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))) : Result n :=
  match order.find? (fun i => (answer δ k cost query i).isNone) with
  | some i => .cut (parts i) (target δ (cost i) - 1)
  | none => .found (combine (fun i => (answer δ k cost query i).getD ∅))

open LinearRelaxation SeparatorComponents
open ComponentCutEncoding

axiom collect_correct {n r : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k h : ℕ) (δ : ℚ) (η : ℝ)
    (hn : 0 < n) (hk : 0 < k) (hδ : 0 < δ) (small : δ ≤ 1 / 4) (hη : 0 < η)
    (x y : MomentVector n r) (feasible : IsFeasible G k r y)
    (A S : Finset (Fin n)) (P : Partition G S ι) (size : A.card ≤ r)
    (moment : η ≤ value y A) (count : Fintype.card ι ≤ 2 * n)
    (light : ∑ v ∈ S, conditioned y A v ≤ (δ : ℝ) * k)
    (order : List ι) (complete : ∀ i, i ∈ order)
    (c : ι → ℚ) (cost_cast : ∀ i, (c i : ℝ) = ∑ v ∈ P.vertices i, conditioned y A v)
    (query : ι → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n)))
    (queries : ∀ i, δ * k / (4 * n) < c i →
      match query i (target δ (c i)) with
      | some I => I ⊆ P.vertices i ∧ G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
          (1 - 4 * (δ : ℝ)) ^ h * (target δ (c i) : ℝ) ≤ I.card
      | none => IsIndependenceBound G (P.vertices i) (target δ (c i) - 1))
    (near : ∀ B, |x B - y B| ≤ η * (δ : ℝ) ^ 2 / (32 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) :
    match collect order P.vertices δ k c query with
    | .found I => G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
        (1 - 4 * (δ : ℝ)) ^ (h + 1) * (k : ℝ) ≤ I.card
    | .cut C u => u ≤ n ∧ IsIndependenceBound G C u ∧
        (∀ z ∈ independentSetHull G k r, evaluate (coefficient A C u) z ≤ 0) ∧
        η * (δ : ℝ) ^ 2 / (16 * n) ≤ evaluate (coefficient A C u) x ∧
        (∑ B : Coordinate n r, |(coefficient A C u B : ℝ)|) ≤ 2 * n

end Lax263307.ComputedRounding

concepts.title: Computing balanced light separators from registered flow-cut outputs
concepts.description:
Label each remaining vertex set in increasing order, construct its rational
split network, and read the cut membership prefix of the registered
Leighton–Rao solver's output. Orient the two projected shores by size.
Repeat until the remainder has at most two thirds of the original vertices.
The computed list has at most n cuts. Its separator has the stated cost,
and its computed pieces form a balanced partition with no cross edges.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
All labels, rational capacities, output decoding, shore choices, and the
bounded cut-list loop are computable. The solver retains its actual registered
RAM polynomial-time guarantee. This statement gives the wrapper's functional correctness.
The main theorem also verifies its RAM implementation and running time.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.EdgeBagBounds
import Lax263307.ForcedSeparation
import Lax263307.CutTraces
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Sort
import Mathlib.Data.List.GetD

/-!
---
title: Computing balanced light separators from registered flow-cut outputs
type: lemma
---
Label each remaining vertex set in increasing order, construct its rational
split network, and read the cut membership prefix of the registered
Leighton–Rao solver's output. Orient the two projected shores by size.
Repeat until the remainder has at most two thirds of the original vertices.
The computed list has at most n cuts. Its separator has the stated cost,
and its computed pieces form a balanced partition with no cross edges.

# Formalization notes

All labels, rational capacities, output decoding, shore choices, and the
bounded cut-list loop are computable. The solver retains its actual registered
RAM polynomial-time guarantee. This statement gives the wrapper's functional correctness.
The main theorem also verifies its RAM implementation and running time.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ComputedSeparators

open EdgeSublinearSeparators (IsBalancedSeparator)
open Lax759944.RamPolytime (RamPolytime)
open SeparatorComponents (Partition)
open scoped NNRat
open VertexSplitting Lax455465.RationalEncoding

def decodeCut (n : ℕ) (words : List ℕ) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun v => words.getD v.val 0 = 1

def label {n : ℕ} (R : Finset (Fin n)) : Fin R.card ↪o Fin n :=
  R.orderEmbOfFin rfl

def restriction {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (R : Finset (Fin n)) :
    SimpleGraph (Fin R.card) := G.comap (label R)

instance {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (R : Finset (Fin n)) :
    DecidableRel (restriction G R).Adj := inferInstanceAs (DecidableRel (G.comap (label R)).Adj)

def ratio (B n : ℕ) : ℚ := B * ((Nat.log2 (2 * n) : ℚ) + 1)
def scale (n ℓ k : ℕ) : ℚ := (ℓ : ℚ) * n ^ 2 / (3 * k)

def largeCapacity (B n r ℓ k : ℕ) : ℚ≥0 :=
  (Nat.ceil (ratio B n * (2 * r : ℕ) ^ 2 / scale n ℓ k) + 1 : ℕ)

def orient {n : ℕ} (A B : Finset (Fin n)) : Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n) :=
  if B.card ≤ A.card then (A, B) else (B, A)

def step {n : ℕ} (solve : List ℕ → List ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (B ℓ k : ℕ) (R : Finset (Fin n)) :
    Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n) :=
  let I := splitInstance (restriction G R) (fun v => x (label R v))
    (largeCapacity B n R.card ℓ k)
  let U := decodeCut (2 * R.card) (solve (encodeInput .directed I))
  let shores := orient (leftShore U) (rightShore U)
  (shores.1.image (label R), shores.2.image (label R))

def cuts {n : ℕ} (cut : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n)) :
    ℕ → Finset (Fin n) → List (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n))
  | 0, _ => []
  | fuel + 1, R =>
    if 3 * R.card ≤ 2 * n then []
    else let s := cut R
      s :: cuts cut fuel (s.1 \ s.2)

def separator {n : ℕ} (cs : List (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n))) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  cs.foldr (fun s S => (s.1 ∩ s.2) ∪ S) ∅

def remaining {n : ℕ} (start : Finset (Fin n))
    (cs : List (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n))) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  if h : cs.length = 0 then start else
    let s := cs.get ⟨cs.length - 1, by omega⟩
    s.1 \ s.2

def pieces {n : ℕ} (cs : List (Finset (Fin n) × Finset (Fin n))) :
    Option (Fin cs.length) → Finset (Fin n)
  | none => remaining Finset.univ cs
  | some i => (cs.get i).2 \ (cs.get i).1

open GraphClasses PowerBagBounds
open Entropy RepeatedCutAccounting

axiom light_separator (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (a A : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hA : 0 < A) (class_bound : HasPowerBagBound C a A) :
    ∃ (solve : List ℕ → List ℕ) (K B : ℕ), RamPolytime solve ∧
      0 < K ∧ 0 < B ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G ∈ C n → 0 < n → ∀ (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (k p ℓ : ℕ),
      0 < k → 0 < p → 0 < ℓ →
      (∀ v, (x v : ℝ) ≤ 1) → (∑ v, (x v : ℝ)) ≤ k →
      edgeCost G (fun v => (x v : ℝ)) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ 2 / p →
      (K : ℝ) * ((ℓ : ℝ) + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2) ≤ k →
      (2 * K : ℝ) * ((ℓ : ℝ) + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2) ≤ p →
      let cs := cuts (step solve G x B ℓ k) n Finset.univ
      cs.length ≤ n ∧
        IsBalancedSeparator G
          (ComputedSeparators.separator cs) ∧
        cost (fun v => (x v : ℝ)) (ComputedSeparators.separator cs) ≤
          12 * (ratio B n : ℝ) * k / ℓ ∧
        ∃ P : Partition G
            (ComputedSeparators.separator cs) (Option (Fin cs.length)),
          (∀ i, P.vertices i = pieces cs i) ∧ ∀ i, 3 * (P.vertices i).card ≤ 2 * n

end Lax263307.ComputedSeparators

                                                          ℓ.cast))
                                                      (Exists fun P =>
                                                        And
                                                          (∀ (i : Option (Fin cs.length)),
                                                            Eq (P.vertices i)
                                                              (Lax263307.ComputedSeparators.pieces cs i))
                                                          (∀ (i : Option (Fin cs.length)),
                                                            instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul 3 (P.vertices i).card)
                                                              (instHMul.hMul 2 n))))))))

concepts.title: Conditioning graph routes on uniform endpoints
concepts.description:
Multiply the probability of a route with endpoints $(u,v)$ by $n^2$ to
obtain the conditional route law for this ordered endpoint pair. Every
conditional law is a probability distribution supported on routes with
those endpoints. Averaging over a uniformly sampled pair recovers the
original law. Averaging independently over four endpoints gives the product
law for two routes. These identities support sampling nonincident source
edges while sharing endpoint images for incident edges.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.RouteDistributions

/-!
---
title: Conditioning graph routes on uniform endpoints
type: lemma
---
Multiply the probability of a route with endpoints $(u,v)$ by $n^2$ to
obtain the conditional route law for this ordered endpoint pair. Every
conditional law is a probability distribution supported on routes with
those endpoints. Averaging over a uniformly sampled pair recovers the
original law. Averaging independently over four endpoints gives the product
law for two routes. These identities support sampling nonincident source
edges while sharing endpoint images for incident edges.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes

open RouteDistributions

noncomputable def conditional {n q : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (u v : Fin n) (i : Fin q) : ℝ :=
  if (D.route i).head? = some u ∧ (D.route i).getLast? = some v then
    (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * D.probability i else 0

axiom conditional_correct {n q : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (u v : Fin n) :
    (∀ i, 0 ≤ conditional D u v i) ∧ (∑ i, conditional D u v i) = 1 ∧
      (∀ i, 0 < conditional D u v i → (D.route i).head? = some u ∧
        (D.route i).getLast? = some v ∧ (D.route i).Nodup ∧ (D.route i).IsChain G.Adj)

axiom mixture_identity {n q : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (i : Fin q) :
    (∑ u, ∑ v, conditional D u v i) = (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * D.probability i

axiom independent_pair_mixture {n q : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (i j : Fin q) :
    (∑ u, ∑ v, ∑ s, ∑ t,
      conditional D u v i * conditional D s t j / (n : ℝ) ^ 4) =
        D.probability i * D.probability j

end Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes

  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    ∀ (u v : Fin n),
      And (∀ (i : Fin q), Real.instLE.le 0 (Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes.conditional D u v i))
        (And (Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun i => Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes.conditional D u v i) 1)
          (∀ (i : Fin q),
            Real.instLT.lt 0 (Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes.conditional D u v i) →
              And (Eq (D.route i).head? (Option.some u))
                (And (Eq (D.route i).getLast? (Option.some v))
                  (And (D.route i).Nodup (List.IsChain G.Adj (D.route i))))))

  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    ∀ (i j : Fin q),
      Eq
        (Finset.univ.sum fun u =>
          Finset.univ.sum fun v =>
            Finset.univ.sum fun s =>
              Finset.univ.sum fun t =>
                instHDiv.hDiv
                  (instHMul.hMul (Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes.conditional D u v i)
                    (Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes.conditional D s t j))
                  (instHPow.hPow n.cast 4))
        (instHMul.hMul (D.probability i) (D.probability j))

  Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun u => Finset.univ.sum fun v => Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes.conditional D u v i)
    (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow n.cast 2) (D.probability i))

concepts.title: Conditioning preserves bounded costs and total mass
concepts.description:
Let $y\in R_r(G,k)$ and let $|A|\le r$ with $y_A>0$.
The conditioned costs $x_v=y_{A\cup\{v\}}/y_A$ lie in $[0,1]$,
sum to $k$, and equal one for every $v\in A$.
Whenever $x_v>0$, the enlarged conditioning set still has positive moment.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.LinearRelaxation

/-!
---
title: Conditioning preserves bounded costs and total mass
type: lemma
---
Let $y\in R_r(G,k)$ and let $|A|\le r$ with $y_A>0$.
The conditioned costs $x_v=y_{A\cup\{v\}}/y_A$ lie in $[0,1]$,
sum to $k$, and equal one for every $v\in A$.
Whenever $x_v>0$, the enlarged conditioning set still has positive moment.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ConditionedCosts

open LinearRelaxation

/-- Basic invariants of the conditioning operation. -/
axiom conditioning_invariants {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k r : ℕ)
    (y : MomentVector n r) (feasible : IsFeasible G k r y)
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (size : A.card ≤ r) (positive : 0 < value y A) :
    (∀ v, 0 ≤ conditioned y A v ∧ conditioned y A v ≤ 1) ∧
    (∑ v : Fin n, conditioned y A v) = k ∧
    (∀ v ∈ A, conditioned y A v = 1) ∧
    (∀ v, 0 < conditioned y A v → 0 < value y (insert v A))

end Lax263307.ConditionedCosts

  Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.IsFeasible G k r y →
    ∀ (A : Finset (Fin n)),
      instLENat.le A.card r →
        Real.instLT.lt 0 (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.value y A) →
          And
            (∀ (v : Fin n),
              And (Real.instLE.le 0 (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.conditioned y A v))
                (Real.instLE.le (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.conditioned y A v) 1))
            (And (Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun v => Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.conditioned y A v) k.cast)
              (And (∀ (v : Fin n), SetLike.instMembership.mem A v → Eq (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.conditioned y A v) 1)
                (∀ (v : Fin n),
                  Real.instLT.lt 0 (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.conditioned y A v) →
                    Real.instLT.lt 0 (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.value y (Finset.instInsert.insert v A)))))
statements.doc: Basic invariants of the conditioning operation.

concepts.title: Joint distributions for the entropy-decrease argument
concepts.description:
For $y\in R_r(G,k)$, $k>0$, $|A|<r$, and $y_A>0$, set
$$\pi_v=\frac{y_{A\cup\{v\}}}{k y_A},\qquad
q_{uv}=\frac{y_{A\cup\{u,v\}}}{k^2 y_A}.$$
The vector $\pi$ is a probability distribution. The entries of $q$ are
nonnegative and symmetric, with both marginals equal to $\pi$, and $q_{uv}=0$
whenever $uv$ is an edge. For $\pi_v>0$, the distribution after conditioning
on $v$ is given by $\pi^v_u=q_{uv}/\pi_v$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.ConditionedCosts

/-!
---
title: Joint distributions for the entropy-decrease argument
type: lemma
---
For $y\in R_r(G,k)$, $k>0$, $|A|<r$, and $y_A>0$, set
$$\pi_v=\frac{y_{A\cup\{v\}}}{k y_A},\qquad
q_{uv}=\frac{y_{A\cup\{u,v\}}}{k^2 y_A}.$$
The vector $\pi$ is a probability distribution. The entries of $q$ are
nonnegative and symmetric, with both marginals equal to $\pi$, and $q_{uv}=0$
whenever $uv$ is an edge. For $\pi_v>0$, the distribution after conditioning
on $v$ is given by $\pi^v_u=q_{uv}/\pi_v$.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution

open LinearRelaxation

/-- Normalize conditioned vertex costs to a probability vector. -/
noncomputable def marginal {n r : ℕ} (y : MomentVector n r)
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (k : ℕ) (v : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  conditioned y A v / k

/-- The joint distribution obtained from moments containing two extra vertices. -/
noncomputable def joint {n r : ℕ} (y : MomentVector n r)
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (k : ℕ) (u v : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  value y (insert u (insert v A)) / ((k : ℝ) ^ 2 * value y A)

/-- The probability and conditional-probability identities for the moment relaxation. -/
axiom distribution_identities {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k r : ℕ)
    (y : MomentVector n r) (feasible : IsFeasible G k r y)
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (size : A.card < r) (positive : 0 < value y A)
    (target_positive : 0 < k) :
    (∀ v, 0 ≤ marginal y A k v) ∧
    (∑ v : Fin n, marginal y A k v) = 1 ∧
    (∀ u v, 0 ≤ joint y A k u v) ∧
    (∀ u v, joint y A k u v = joint y A k v u) ∧
    (∀ v, (∑ u : Fin n, joint y A k u v) = marginal y A k v) ∧
    (∀ u v, G.Adj u v → joint y A k u v = 0) ∧
    (∀ u v, 0 < marginal y A k v →
      marginal y (insert v A) k u = joint y A k u v / marginal y A k v)

end Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution

  Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.IsFeasible G k r y →
    ∀ (A : Finset (Fin n)),
      instLTNat.lt A.card r →
        Real.instLT.lt 0 (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.value y A) →
          instLTNat.lt 0 k →
            And (∀ (v : Fin n), Real.instLE.le 0 (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.marginal y A k v))
              (And (Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun v => Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.marginal y A k v) 1)
                (And (∀ (u v : Fin n), Real.instLE.le 0 (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.joint y A k u v))
                  (And
                    (∀ (u v : Fin n),
                      Eq (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.joint y A k u v)
                        (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.joint y A k v u))
                    (And
                      (∀ (v : Fin n),
                        Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun u => Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.joint y A k u v)
                          (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.marginal y A k v))
                      (And (∀ (u v : Fin n), G.Adj u v → Eq (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.joint y A k u v) 0)
                        (∀ (u v : Fin n),
                          Real.instLT.lt 0 (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.marginal y A k v) →
                            Eq (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.marginal y (Finset.instInsert.insert v A) k u)
                              (instHDiv.hDiv (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.joint y A k u v)
                                (Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution.marginal y A k v))))))))

concepts.title: Bags meeting a connected vertex set
concepts.description:
In a tree decomposition, the nodes whose bags meet a nonempty connected
vertex set induce a connected subtree. The bag subtrees of adjacent vertices
intersect in a bag covering their edge, so connected vertex sets give
connected unions of bag subtrees.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax228581.Treewidth
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Fin

/-!
---
title: Bags meeting a connected vertex set
type: lemma
---
In a tree decomposition, the nodes whose bags meet a nonempty connected
vertex set induce a connected subtree. The bag subtrees of adjacent vertices
intersect in a bag covering their edge, so connected vertex sets give
connected unions of bag subtrees.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ConnectedBags

open Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- The decomposition nodes whose bags meet `U`. -/
def meetingNodes {n : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : TreeDecomposition G) (U : Finset (Fin n)) : Set D.Node :=
  {i | ∃ v ∈ U, v ∈ D.bag i}

/-- Connected vertex sets meet a connected collection of decomposition bags. -/
axiom meeting_connected {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (D : TreeDecomposition G) (U : Finset (Fin n))
    (connected : (G.induce (↑U : Set (Fin n))).Connected) :
    (D.tree.induce (meetingNodes D U)).Connected

end Lax263307.ConnectedBags

statements.signature:
meeting_connected : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (D : Lax228581.Treewidth.TreeDecomposition G) (U : Finset (Fin n)),
  (SimpleGraph.induce (Finset.instSetLike.coe U) G).Connected →
    (SimpleGraph.induce (Lax263307.ConnectedBags.meetingNodes D U) D.tree).Connected
statements.doc: Connected vertex sets meet a connected collection of decomposition bags.

concepts.title: Tree-decomposition transfer through connected vertex representations
concepts.description:
Represent each vertex of $H$ by a nonempty connected vertex set of $G$, with
intersecting sets for every edge of $H$. Suppose at most $B$ represented
vertices use any one vertex of $G$. A tree decomposition of $G$ with bags
of size at most $w$ then gives a tree decomposition of $H$ with bags of
size at most $Bw$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.ConnectedBags

/-!
---
title: Tree-decomposition transfer through connected vertex representations
type: lemma
---
Represent each vertex of $H$ by a nonempty connected vertex set of $G$, with
intersecting sets for every edge of $H$. Suppose at most $B$ represented
vertices use any one vertex of $G$. A tree decomposition of $G$ with bags
of size at most $w$ then gives a tree decomposition of $H$ with bags of
size at most $Bw$.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ConnectedRepresentations

open Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- A connected vertex set in `G` for each vertex of `H`. -/
structure Representation {t n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t))
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) where
  /-- The vertices used by a represented vertex. -/
  carrier : Fin t → Finset (Fin n)
  /-- Each carrier is nonempty and connected. -/
  connected : ∀ v, (G.induce (↑(carrier v) : Set (Fin n))).Connected
  /-- Carriers of adjacent vertices intersect. -/
  touching : ∀ u v, H.Adj u v → ∃ a, a ∈ carrier u ∧ a ∈ carrier v

/-- Which represented vertices use a particular host vertex. -/
def users {t n : ℕ} {H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (R : Representation H G) (a : Fin n) : Finset (Fin t) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun v => a ∈ R.carrier v

/-- Transfer a decomposition with a uniform bound on the representation load. -/
axiom transfer_decomposition {t n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t))
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (R : Representation H G)
    (B w : ℕ) (load_bound : ∀ a, (users R a).card ≤ B)
    (D : TreeDecomposition G) (bag_bound : ∀ i, (D.bag i).card ≤ w) :
    ∃ D' : TreeDecomposition H, ∀ i, (D'.bag i).card ≤ B * w

end Lax263307.ConnectedRepresentations

statements.signature:
transfer_decomposition : ∀ {t n : Nat} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
  (R : Lax263307.ConnectedRepresentations.Representation H G) (B w : Nat),
  (∀ (a : Fin n), instLENat.le (Lax263307.ConnectedRepresentations.users R a).card B) →
    ∀ (D : Lax228581.Treewidth.TreeDecomposition G),
      (∀ (i : D.Node), instLENat.le (D.bag i).card w) →
        Exists fun D' => ∀ (i : D'.Node), instLENat.le (D'.bag i).card (instHMul.hMul B w)
statements.doc: Transfer a decomposition with a uniform bound on the representation load.

concepts.title: A computable catalog and index for moment coordinates
concepts.description:
Enumerate only subsets of size at most r+2, remove duplicates, and attach
the cardinality proof to each entry. This lists each moment coordinate
exactly once and gives a computable equivalence between coordinate indices
and the coordinate type. The catalog has at most (r+3)(n+1)^(r+2) entries.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The inverse index uses list search. This avoids a choice-based Fintype
equivalence in LP input construction. Duplicate removal is permitted as
its polynomial overhead in the catalogue length fits the quasipolynomial
bound. The proof package implements this enumeration on the RAM.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.RationalConditioning
import Mathlib.Data.List.NodupEquivFin
import Mathlib.Data.List.Dedup

/-!
---
title: A computable catalog and index for moment coordinates
type: lemma
---
Enumerate only subsets of size at most r+2, remove duplicates, and attach
the cardinality proof to each entry. This lists each moment coordinate
exactly once and gives a computable equivalence between coordinate indices
and the coordinate type. The catalog has at most (r+3)(n+1)^(r+2) entries.

# Formalization notes

The inverse index uses list search. This avoids a choice-based Fintype
equivalence in LP input construction. Duplicate removal is permitted as
its polynomial overhead in the catalogue length fits the quasipolynomial
bound. The proof package implements this enumeration on the RAM.
-/

namespace Lax263307.CoordinateCatalog

open LinearRelaxation RationalConditioning

private theorem candidate_complete_aux (n r : ℕ) (A : Finset (Fin n)) :
    A ∈ candidates n r ↔ A.card ≤ r := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨j, hj, hm⟩ := List.mem_flatMap.mp h
    obtain ⟨l, hl, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hm
    have hsub := (List.mem_sublistsLen.mp hl).1
    have hlen := (List.mem_sublistsLen.mp hl).2
    have hnd := hsub.nodup (List.nodup_finRange n)
    rw [List.toFinset_card_of_nodup hnd, hlen]
    have := List.mem_range.mp hj
    omega
  · intro hA
    let l := (List.finRange n).filter fun v => decide (v ∈ A)
    have hsub : List.Sublist l (List.finRange n) := List.filter_sublist
    have hnd : l.Nodup := hsub.nodup (List.nodup_finRange n)
    have heq : l.toFinset = A := by ext v; simp [l]
    have hlen : l.length = A.card := by rw [← List.toFinset_card_of_nodup hnd, heq]
    apply List.mem_flatMap.mpr
    refine ⟨A.card, List.mem_range.mpr (by omega), ?_⟩
    apply List.mem_map.mpr
    exact ⟨l, List.mem_sublistsLen.mpr ⟨hsub, hlen⟩, heq⟩

def sets (n r : ℕ) : List (Finset (Fin n)) := (candidates n (r + 2)).dedup

def catalog (n r : ℕ) : List (Coordinate n r) :=
  (sets n r).attach.map (fun A => ⟨A.val,
    (candidate_complete_aux n (r + 2) A.val).mp
      (List.mem_dedup.mp A.property)⟩)

axiom catalog_complete (n r : ℕ) (A : Coordinate n r) : A ∈ catalog n r

private theorem catalog_complete_aux (n r : ℕ) (A : Coordinate n r) : A ∈ catalog n r := by
  have hmem : A.val ∈ sets n r :=
    List.mem_dedup.mpr ((candidate_complete_aux n (r + 2) A.val).mpr A.property)
  apply List.mem_map.mpr
  exact ⟨⟨A.val, hmem⟩, List.mem_attach _ _, Subtype.ext rfl⟩

private theorem catalog_nodup_aux (n r : ℕ) : (catalog n r).Nodup := by
  have hnd : (sets n r).Nodup := List.nodup_dedup _
  apply hnd.attach.map
  intro A B h
  exact Subtype.ext (congrArg (fun C : Coordinate n r => C.val) h)

def indexing (n r : ℕ) : Fin (catalog n r).length ≃ Coordinate n r :=
  List.Nodup.getEquivOfForallMemList (catalog n r) (catalog_nodup_aux n r) (catalog_complete_aux n r)

axiom catalog_bound (n r : ℕ) : (catalog n r).length ≤ (r + 3) * (n + 1) ^ (r + 2)

axiom catalog_positive (n r : ℕ) : 0 < (catalog n r).length

axiom catalog_two (n r : ℕ) (positive : 0 < n) : 2 ≤ (catalog n r).length

end Lax263307.CoordinateCatalog

  instLENat.le (Lax263307.CoordinateCatalog.catalog n r).length
    (instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd r 3) (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd n 1) (instHAdd.hAdd r 2)))

concepts.title: A width obstruction from sparse costs and bounded route loads
concepts.description:
Assume vertex costs lie in $[0,1]$, have total mass at most $k>0$, and
edge cost at most $k^2/p$. A route distribution with vertex loads at most
$\ell x_v/k$ satisfies the sampling budgets for any source graph with
$m$ edges when $k\ge8m^2\ell^2$ and $p\ge16m^2\ell^2$.
Consequently, for a source graph of maximum degree $d$, a monotone class
bag bound $W$ forces a discarded-edge count $q$ with
$Lq\le4m\ell$ and the pruned source treewidth-plus-one bound.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The class bag bound is an explicit intermediate hypothesis. This lemma
combines the probability estimates with the sampled width obstruction.
The main theorem obtains the bag bound from its separator hypothesis.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.InducedEmbeddingWidth

/-!
---
title: A width obstruction from sparse costs and bounded route loads
type: lemma
---
Assume vertex costs lie in $[0,1]$, have total mass at most $k>0$, and
edge cost at most $k^2/p$. A route distribution with vertex loads at most
$\ell x_v/k$ satisfies the sampling budgets for any source graph with
$m$ edges when $k\ge8m^2\ell^2$ and $p\ge16m^2\ell^2$.
Consequently, for a source graph of maximum degree $d$, a monotone class
bag bound $W$ forces a discarded-edge count $q$ with
$Lq\le4m\ell$ and the pruned source treewidth-plus-one bound.

# Formalization notes

The class bag bound is an explicit intermediate hypothesis. This lemma
combines the probability estimates with the sampled width obstruction.
The main theorem obtains the bag bound from its separator hypothesis.
-/

namespace Lax263307.CostSamplingObstruction

open Entropy (edgeCost)
open PathSampling (load)
open RouteDistributions (Distribution)
open GraphClasses InducedEmbeddingWidth Lax228581.Treewidth

axiom cost_width_obstruction {t n q : ℕ} (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (W : ℕ → ℕ) (monotone : Monotone W) (class_bound : HasBagBound C W)
    (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (member : G ∈ C n) (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n)
    (d L : ℕ) (degree_bound : ∀ v, H.degree v ≤ d) (edge_positive : 0 < H.edgeSet.ncard)
    (x : Fin n → ℝ) (k ℓ p : ℝ) (k_positive : 0 < k) (ℓ_positive : 0 < ℓ) (p_positive : 0 < p)
    (cost_bounds : ∀ v, 0 ≤ x v ∧ x v ≤ 1) (mass : (∑ v, x v) ≤ k)
    (load_bound : ∀ v, load D.toSampling v ≤ ℓ * x v / k)
    (edge_bound : edgeCost G x ≤ k ^ 2 / p)
    (target_large : 8 * (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ 2 * ℓ ^ 2 ≤ k)
    (sparsity_large : 16 * (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ 2 * ℓ ^ 2 ≤ p) :
    ∃ removed : ℕ, (L : ℝ) * removed ≤ 4 * (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) * ℓ ∧
      treewidth H + 1 ≤ max 1 (2 * d * W (d * H.edgeSet.ncard * L ^ 2)) + removed

end Lax263307.CostSamplingObstruction

statements.signature:
cost_width_obstruction : ∀ {t n q : Nat} (C : Lax263307.GraphClasses.GraphClass),
  Lax263307.GraphClasses.IsHereditary C →
    ∀ (W : Nat → Nat),
      Monotone W →

concepts.title: Coupled route sampling with shared vertex images
concepts.description:
Choose independently a uniform image for every source vertex, then sample
one graph route per source edge from its conditional endpoint law. Positive
outcomes give every route the chosen images of its source endpoints.
Each edge's route has the original route distribution. Routes of two
nonincident source edges have its independent product law, because the four
source endpoints have independently chosen images.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The finite outcome is a pair consisting of a source-vertex image assignment
and a route-index assignment. Edge endpoints are given explicitly by two
maps; the marginal assertions require distinct endpoints for a single edge
and four distinct endpoints for a pair. The construction does not assume
independence for incident source edges.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.ConditionalRoutes
import Lax263307.FiniteProductSampling

/-!
---
title: Coupled route sampling with shared vertex images
type: lemma
---
Choose independently a uniform image for every source vertex, then sample
one graph route per source edge from its conditional endpoint law. Positive
outcomes give every route the chosen images of its source endpoints.
Each edge's route has the original route distribution. Routes of two
nonincident source edges have its independent product law, because the four
source endpoints have independently chosen images.

# Formalization notes

The finite outcome is a pair consisting of a source-vertex image assignment
and a route-index assignment. Edge endpoints are given explicitly by two
maps; the marginal assertions require distinct endpoints for a single edge
and four distinct endpoints for a pair. The construction does not assume
independence for incident source edges.
-/

namespace Lax263307.CoupledRouteSampling

open RouteDistributions ConditionalRoutes
open FiniteProductSampling

noncomputable def uniformWeight (n : ℕ) : Fin n → ℝ := fun _ => 1 / (n : ℝ)

noncomputable def jointWeight {n q t m : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (a b : Fin m → Fin t)
    (φ : Fin t → Fin n) (ψ : Fin m → Fin q) : ℝ :=
  weight (fun _ : Fin t => uniformWeight n) φ *
    weight (fun e => conditional D (φ (a e)) (φ (b e))) ψ

axiom joint_normalized {n q t m : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (a b : Fin m → Fin t) :
    (∀ φ ψ, 0 ≤ jointWeight D a b φ ψ) ∧
      (∑ φ, ∑ ψ, jointWeight D a b φ ψ) = 1

axiom joint_valid {n q t m : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (a b : Fin m → Fin t)
    (φ : Fin t → Fin n) (ψ : Fin m → Fin q) (positive : 0 < jointWeight D a b φ ψ) :
    ∀ e, (D.route (ψ e)).head? = some (φ (a e)) ∧
      (D.route (ψ e)).getLast? = some (φ (b e)) ∧
      (D.route (ψ e)).Nodup ∧ (D.route (ψ e)).IsChain G.Adj

axiom single_edge_law {n q t m : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (a b : Fin m → Fin t)
    (e : Fin m) (nonloop : a e ≠ b e) (i : Fin q) :
    (∑ φ, ∑ ψ, jointWeight D a b φ ψ * (if ψ e = i then (1 : ℝ) else 0)) =
      D.probability i

axiom nonincident_edge_law {n q t m : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (a b : Fin m → Fin t)
    (e f : Fin m) (nonincident : Function.Injective ![a e, b e, a f, b f]) (i j : Fin q) :
    (∑ φ, ∑ ψ, jointWeight D a b φ ψ *
      ((if ψ e = i then (1 : ℝ) else 0) * (if ψ f = j then (1 : ℝ) else 0))) =
      D.probability i * D.probability j

end Lax263307.CoupledRouteSampling

  instLTNat.lt 0 n →

      And
        (∀ (φ : Fin t → Fin n) (ψ : Fin m → Fin q),

        (Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun φ => Finset.univ.sum fun ψ => Lax263307.CoupledRouteSampling.jointWeight D a b φ ψ) 1)

  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    ∀ (a b : Fin m → Fin t) (φ : Fin t → Fin n) (ψ : Fin m → Fin q),

        ∀ (e : Fin m),

    ∀ (a b : Fin m → Fin t) (e f : Fin m),
      Function.Injective
          (Matrix.vecCons (a e) (Matrix.vecCons (b e) (Matrix.vecCons (a f) (Matrix.vecCons (b f) Matrix.vecEmpty)))) →
        ∀ (i j : Fin q),
          Eq
            (Finset.univ.sum fun φ =>
              Finset.univ.sum fun ψ =>
                instHMul.hMul (Lax263307.CoupledRouteSampling.jointWeight D a b φ ψ)
                  (instHMul.hMul (ite (Eq (ψ e) i) 1 0) (ite (Eq (ψ f) j) 1 0)))
            (instHMul.hMul (D.probability i) (D.probability j))

  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    ∀ (a b : Fin m → Fin t) (e : Fin m),
      Ne (a e) (b e) →
        ∀ (i : Fin q),
          Eq
            (Finset.univ.sum fun φ =>
              Finset.univ.sum fun ψ =>
                instHMul.hMul (Lax263307.CoupledRouteSampling.jointWeight D a b φ ψ) (ite (Eq (ψ e) i) 1 0))
            (D.probability i)

concepts.title: A good coupled sample with bounded total route size
concepts.description:
For a source graph with $m$ edges, the expected total sampled route size is
$m$ times the single-route expectation. The probability that some pair of
nonincident routes intersects or has a host edge between them is at most
$m^2$ times the sum of the single-pair collision and adjacency probabilities.
If that bound is at most $1/4$ and the expected total size is at most $M>0$,
there is a positive-probability sample with no such interaction and total
route size at most $4M$.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.CoupledRouteSampling
import Lax263307.SamplingOutcomes

/-!
---
title: A good coupled sample with bounded total route size
type: lemma
---
For a source graph with $m$ edges, the expected total sampled route size is
$m$ times the single-route expectation. The probability that some pair of
nonincident routes intersects or has a host edge between them is at most
$m^2$ times the sum of the single-pair collision and adjacency probabilities.
If that bound is at most $1/4$ and the expected total size is at most $M>0$,
there is a positive-probability sample with no such interaction and total
route size at most $4M$.
-/

namespace Lax263307.CoupledSamplingBounds

open PathSampling (adjacencyProbability collisionProbability expectedSize)
open RouteDistributions CoupledRouteSampling

noncomputable def Interaction {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (D : Distribution G q) (i j : Fin q) : Prop :=
  ¬Disjoint (D.route i).toFinset (D.route j).toFinset ∨
    ∃ u ∈ (D.route i).toFinset, ∃ v ∈ (D.route j).toFinset, G.Adj u v

noncomputable instance {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (D : Distribution G q) (i j : Fin q) : Decidable (Interaction G D i j) := Classical.propDecidable _

noncomputable def badProbability {n q t m : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (D : Distribution G q) (a b : Fin m → Fin t) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ φ, ∑ ψ, if ∃ e f, Function.Injective ![a e, b e, a f, b f] ∧ Interaction G D (ψ e) (ψ f)
    then jointWeight D a b φ ψ else 0

axiom total_length_expectation {n q t m : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (a b : Fin m → Fin t)
    (nonloop : ∀ e, a e ≠ b e) :
    (∑ φ, ∑ ψ, jointWeight D a b φ ψ * (∑ e, ((D.route (ψ e)).toFinset.card : ℝ))) =
      (m : ℝ) * expectedSize D.toSampling

axiom bad_probability_bound {n q t m : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (a b : Fin m → Fin t) :
    badProbability G D a b ≤ (m : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      (collisionProbability D.toSampling +
        adjacencyProbability G D.toSampling)

axiom good_route_sample {n q t m : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n) (a b : Fin m → Fin t) (nonloop : ∀ e, a e ≠ b e)
    (M : ℝ) (positive : 0 < M)
    (bad_budget : (m : ℝ) ^ 2 * (collisionProbability D.toSampling +
      adjacencyProbability G D.toSampling) ≤ 1 / 4)
    (length_budget : (m : ℝ) * expectedSize D.toSampling ≤ M) :
    ∃ φ : Fin t → Fin n, ∃ ψ : Fin m → Fin q,
      0 < jointWeight D a b φ ψ ∧
      (∀ e f, Function.Injective ![a e, b e, a f, b f] → ¬Interaction G D (ψ e) (ψ f)) ∧
      (∑ e, ((D.route (ψ e)).toFinset.card : ℝ)) ≤ 4 * M

end Lax263307.CoupledSamplingBounds

  (D : Lax263307.RouteDistributions.Distribution G q),
  instLTNat.lt 0 n →
    ∀ (a b : Fin m → Fin t),
      Real.instLE.le (Lax263307.CoupledSamplingBounds.badProbability G D a b)
        (instHMul.hMul (instHPow.hPow m.cast 2)
          (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax263307.PathSampling.collisionProbability D.toSampling)
            (Lax263307.PathSampling.adjacencyProbability G D.toSampling)))

    ∀ (a b : Fin m → Fin t),

concepts.title: Repeated cuts yield a balanced light separator
concepts.description:
Record a cut sequence that removes its right shore at each step. Its
separator is the union of shore intersections; its retained parts are the
exclusive discarded pieces and the final remainder. The right shores are
disjoint, each cut removes a nonempty shore, and no graph edge joins distinct
retained parts. Once the final remainder has at most two thirds of the
original order, the separator is balanced and its cost obeys the cumulative
cut bound. There are at most $n$ cuts.

A cut oracle on every remainder above that size threshold produces such a
trace by induction on remainder cardinality.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The small-piece condition bounds $B_i\setminus A_i$, not the full discarded
shore $B_i$, which also contains the separator intersection. The final
parts form the concrete partition used by recursive rounding. These
statements analyze the finite cut sequence; its RAM implementation remains
part of the main algorithm assembly.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.BalancedPartitions
import Lax263307.RepeatedCutAccounting

/-!
---
title: Repeated cuts yield a balanced light separator
type: lemma
---
Record a cut sequence that removes its right shore at each step. Its
separator is the union of shore intersections; its retained parts are the
exclusive discarded pieces and the final remainder. The right shores are
disjoint, each cut removes a nonempty shore, and no graph edge joins distinct
retained parts. Once the final remainder has at most two thirds of the
original order, the separator is balanced and its cost obeys the cumulative
cut bound. There are at most $n$ cuts.

A cut oracle on every remainder above that size threshold produces such a
trace by induction on remainder cardinality.

# Formalization notes

The small-piece condition bounds $B_i\setminus A_i$, not the full discarded
shore $B_i$, which also contains the separator intersection. The final
parts form the concrete partition used by recursive rounding. These
statements analyze the finite cut sequence; its RAM implementation remains
part of the main algorithm assembly.
-/

namespace Lax263307.CutTraces

open RepeatedCutAccounting (cost)
open SeparatorComponents EdgeSublinearSeparators

structure Trace {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (start : Finset (Fin n)) (steps : ℕ) where
  remaining : ℕ → Finset (Fin n)
  left : ℕ → Finset (Fin n)
  right : ℕ → Finset (Fin n)
  initial : remaining 0 = start
  cover : ∀ i < steps, left i ∪ right i = remaining i
  next : ∀ i < steps, remaining (i + 1) = left i \ right i
  nonempty : ∀ i < steps, (right i).Nonempty
  small_piece : ∀ i < steps, 2 * (right i \ left i).card ≤ (remaining i).card
  separated : ∀ i < steps, ∀ u ∈ left i \ right i, ∀ v ∈ right i \ left i, ¬G.Adj u v

noncomputable def separator {n q : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)} {start : Finset (Fin n)}
    (T : Trace G start q) : Finset (Fin n) := Finset.univ.biUnion fun i : Fin q => T.left i ∩ T.right i

def parts {n q : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)} {start : Finset (Fin n)}
    (T : Trace G start q) : Option (Fin q) → Finset (Fin n)
  | none => T.remaining q
  | some i => T.right i \ T.left i

axiom trace_correct {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (T : Trace G Finset.univ q)
    (finished : 3 * (T.remaining q).card ≤ 2 * n)
    (x : Fin n → ℝ) (nonnegative : ∀ v, 0 ≤ x v) (ρ γ : ℝ) (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (each_cut : ∀ i < q, cost x (T.left i ∩ T.right i) ≤
      4 * ρ * (T.left i).card * (T.right i).card / γ) :
    q ≤ n ∧ IsBalancedSeparator G (separator T) ∧
      cost x (separator T) ≤ 4 * ρ * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 / γ

end Lax263307.CutTraces

  instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul 3 (T.remaining q).card) (instHMul.hMul 2 n) →
    ∀ (x : Fin n → Real),
      (∀ (v : Fin n), Real.instLE.le 0 (x v)) →
        ∀ (ρ γ : Real),
          Real.instLE.le 0 ρ →
            Real.instLT.lt 0 γ →
              (∀ (i : Nat),
                  instLTNat.lt i q →
                    Real.instLE.le
                      (Lax263307.RepeatedCutAccounting.cost x (Finset.instInter.inter (T.left i) (T.right i)))
                      (instHDiv.hDiv
                        (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 4 ρ) (T.left i).card.cast) (T.right i).card.cast)
                        γ)) →
                And (instLENat.le q n)
                  (And (Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators.IsBalancedSeparator G (Lax263307.CutTraces.separator T))
                    (Real.instLE.le (Lax263307.RepeatedCutAccounting.cost x (Lax263307.CutTraces.separator T))
                      (instHDiv.hDiv (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul 4 ρ) (instHPow.hPow n.cast 2)) γ)))

concepts.title: Infinity-distance projection LP and its separating dual
concepts.description:
Append one nonnegative distance variable t to a linear program and impose
|y_j-center_j|≤t for every coordinate. Maximizing -t finds a nearest feasible
point. A matching dual certificate supplies a separating normal whose sum
of absolute coefficients is at most one, and its gap at the queried center
is exactly t. Thus a distance threshold yields either a nearby feasible
point for round-or-cut or a uniformly strong separation.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Rows and variables use computable finite index concatenation. No choice-based
coordinate labeling is needed to form the dense rational program. The
algebra holds in real variables and applies to exact rational certificates
by casting. It makes no full-dimensionality assumption. The proof package
implements the matrix construction and registered solver invocation on the RAM.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax109476.RationalCertificates

/-!
---
title: Infinity-distance projection LP and its separating dual
type: lemma
---
Append one nonnegative distance variable t to a linear program and impose
|y_j-center_j|≤t for every coordinate. Maximizing -t finds a nearest feasible
point. A matching dual certificate supplies a separating normal whose sum
of absolute coefficients is at most one, and its gap at the queried center
is exactly t. Thus a distance threshold yields either a nearby feasible
point for round-or-cut or a uniformly strong separation.

# Formalization notes

Rows and variables use computable finite index concatenation. No choice-based
coordinate labeling is needed to form the dense rational program. The
algebra holds in real variables and applies to exact rational certificates
by casting. It makes no full-dimensionality assumption. The proof package
implements the matrix construction and registered solver invocation on the RAM.
-/

namespace Lax263307.DistanceProjection

open Lax109476.LinearProgram

/-- The distance LP with one additional variable and two rows per coordinate. -/
def distanceProgram {K : Type} [Ring K] {m n : ℕ} (P : Program K m n) (center : Fin n → K) :
    Program K (m + (n + n)) (n + 1) where
  A := Fin.addCases
    (fun i => Fin.addCases (P.A i) (fun _ => 0))
    (Fin.addCases
      (fun i => Fin.addCases (fun j => if i = j then 1 else 0) (fun _ => -1))
      (fun i => Fin.addCases (fun j => if i = j then -1 else 0) (fun _ => -1)))
  b := Fin.addCases P.b (Fin.addCases center (fun i => -center i))
  c := Fin.addCases (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => -1)

def point {K : Type} {n : ℕ} (z : Fin (n + 1) → K) (j : Fin n) : K := z (Fin.castAdd 1 j)
def distance {K : Type} {n : ℕ} (z : Fin (n + 1) → K) : K := z (Fin.natAdd n (0 : Fin 1))

def oldMultipliers {K : Type} {m n : ℕ} (dual : Fin (m + (n + n)) → K) (i : Fin m) : K :=
  dual (Fin.castAdd (n + n) i)
def plusMultipliers {K : Type} {m n : ℕ} (dual : Fin (m + (n + n)) → K) (i : Fin n) : K :=
  dual (Fin.natAdd m (Fin.castAdd n i))
def minusMultipliers {K : Type} {m n : ℕ} (dual : Fin (m + (n + n)) → K) (i : Fin n) : K :=
  dual (Fin.natAdd m (Fin.natAdd n i))
def normal {K : Type} [Sub K] {m n : ℕ} (dual : Fin (m + (n + n)) → K) (i : Fin n) : K :=
  minusMultipliers dual i - plusMultipliers dual i

axiom primal_characterization {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℝ m n) (center : Fin n → ℝ)
    (z : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) :
    PrimalFeasible (distanceProgram P center) z ↔
      PrimalFeasible P (point z) ∧ 0 ≤ distance z ∧
        ∀ j, |point z j - center j| ≤ distance z

axiom objective_bounded {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℝ m n) (center : Fin n → ℝ) :
    IsBoundedAbove (distanceProgram P center)

axiom projection_feasible_iff {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℝ m n) (center : Fin n → ℝ) :
    IsFeasible (distanceProgram P center) ↔ IsFeasible P

axiom dual_normal {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℝ m n) (center : Fin n → ℝ)
    (dual : Fin (m + (n + n)) → ℝ) (feasible : DualFeasible (distanceProgram P center) dual) :
    (∑ j, |normal dual j|) ≤ 1 ∧
      ∀ z, PrimalFeasible P z → (∑ j, normal dual j * z j) ≤ dualValue P (oldMultipliers dual)

axiom optimal_gap {m n : ℕ} (P : Program ℝ m n) (center : Fin n → ℝ)
    (z : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (dual : Fin (m + (n + n)) → ℝ)
    (primal : PrimalFeasible (distanceProgram P center) z)
    (dual_feasible : DualFeasible (distanceProgram P center) dual)
    (matching : primalValue (distanceProgram P center) z = dualValue (distanceProgram P center) dual) :
    PrimalFeasible P (point z) ∧ 0 ≤ distance z ∧
      (∀ j, |point z j - center j| ≤ distance z) ∧
      (∑ j, |normal dual j|) ≤ 1 ∧
      (∀ y, PrimalFeasible P y → (∑ j, normal dual j * y j) ≤ dualValue P (oldMultipliers dual)) ∧
      (∑ j, normal dual j * center j) - dualValue P (oldMultipliers dual) = distance z

end Lax263307.DistanceProjection
