dual_normal : ∀ {m n : Nat} (P : Lax109476.LinearProgram.Program Real m n) (center : Fin n → Real)
  (dual : Fin (instHAdd.hAdd m (instHAdd.hAdd n n)) → Real),
  Lax109476.LinearProgram.DualFeasible (Lax263307.DistanceProjection.distanceProgram P center) dual →
    And (Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun j => abs (Lax263307.DistanceProjection.normal dual j)) 1)
      (∀ (z : Fin n → Real),
        Lax109476.LinearProgram.PrimalFeasible P z →
          Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun j => instHMul.hMul (Lax263307.DistanceProjection.normal dual j) (z j))
            (Lax109476.LinearProgram.dualValue P (Lax263307.DistanceProjection.oldMultipliers dual)))

objective_bounded : ∀ {m n : Nat} (P : Lax109476.LinearProgram.Program Real m n) (center : Fin n → Real),
  Lax109476.LinearProgram.IsBoundedAbove (Lax263307.DistanceProjection.distanceProgram P center)

concepts.title: Edge-sublinear separators imply edge-sublinear decomposition bags
concepts.description:
In a hereditary graph class, recursively balanced separators build tree
decompositions with a logarithmic factor. Removing isolated vertices first
bounds the remaining order by twice the edge count. Absorb the logarithm
into a positive fraction of the gap between the separator exponent and one.
The resulting bag bound remains strongly sublinear in the edge count.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
This derives the decomposition bound from the original separator hypothesis.
It uses singleton leaf
bags to restore arbitrarily many isolated vertices. Constants are existential
class constants, as in the main theorem.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.SeparatorDecompositions
import Lax263307.PowerBagBounds

/-!
---
title: Edge-sublinear separators imply edge-sublinear decomposition bags
type: lemma
---
In a hereditary graph class, recursively balanced separators build tree
decompositions with a logarithmic factor. Removing isolated vertices first
bounds the remaining order by twice the edge count. Absorb the logarithm
into a positive fraction of the gap between the separator exponent and one.
The resulting bag bound remains strongly sublinear in the edge count.

# Formalization notes

This derives the decomposition bound from the original separator hypothesis.
It uses singleton leaf
bags to restore arbitrarily many isolated vertices. Constants are existential
class constants, as in the main theorem.
-/

namespace Lax263307.EdgeBagBounds

open GraphClasses EdgeSublinearSeparators Lax228581.Treewidth

axiom sublinear_bag_bound (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (separators : HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C) :
    ∃ β c : ℝ, 0 ≤ β ∧ β < 1 ∧ 0 < c ∧ ∀ n (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ C n →
      ∃ D : TreeDecomposition G, ∀ j,
        ((D.bag j).card : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.rpow ((G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) + 1) β

end Lax263307.EdgeBagBounds

statements.signature:
sublinear_bag_bound : ∀ (C : Lax263307.GraphClasses.GraphClass),
  Lax263307.GraphClasses.IsHereditary C →
    Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators.HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C →
      Exists fun β =>
        Exists fun c =>
          And (Real.instLE.le 0 β)
            (And (Real.instLT.lt β 1)
              (And (Real.instLT.lt 0 c)
                (∀ (n : Nat) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
                  Set.instMembership.mem (C n) G →
                    Exists fun D =>
                      ∀ (j : D.Node),
                        Real.instLE.le (D.bag j).card.cast
                          (instHMul.hMul c ((instHAdd.hAdd G.edgeSet.ncard.cast 1).rpow β)))))

concepts.title: Treewidth loss under edge deletion
concepts.description:
Deleting $q$ edges reduces treewidth by at most $q$. Choose one endpoint of
each deleted edge and add all chosen vertices to every bag of a decomposition
of the remaining graph. This restores edge coverage and increases bag sizes
by at most $q$.

concepts.title: Strongly edge-sublinear separators
concepts.description:
A balanced separator of an $n$-vertex graph $G$ is a vertex set $S$ such
that every connected component of $G-S$ has at most $2n/3$ vertices.
A graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if there are constants
$c>0$ and $0\le b<1$ such that each of its $m$-edge graphs has a balanced
separator of size at most $c(m+1)^b$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The $+1$ makes the paper's asymptotic bound $O(m^b)$ meaningful at $m=0$:
a singleton graph needs a separator of size one under the stated balance
condition. For $m\ge1$ this normalization is equivalent to $O(m^b)$;
edgeless graphs of order at least two have an empty balanced separator.
Edges are counted as unordered pairs, using mathlib's edge set.
The balance inequality uses integers, $3|K|\le2n$, without rounding.
Heredity is a separate hypothesis in the main theorem.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.GraphClasses
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Connected
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

/-!
---
title: Strongly edge-sublinear separators
type: definition
---
A balanced separator of an $n$-vertex graph $G$ is a vertex set $S$ such
that every connected component of $G-S$ has at most $2n/3$ vertices.
A graph class has strongly edge-sublinear separators if there are constants
$c>0$ and $0\le b<1$ such that each of its $m$-edge graphs has a balanced
separator of size at most $c(m+1)^b$.

# Formalization notes

The $+1$ makes the paper's asymptotic bound $O(m^b)$ meaningful at $m=0$:
a singleton graph needs a separator of size one under the stated balance
condition. For $m\ge1$ this normalization is equivalent to $O(m^b)$;
edgeless graphs of order at least two have an empty balanced separator.
Edges are counted as unordered pairs, using mathlib's edge set.
The balance inequality uses integers, $3|K|\le2n$, without rounding.
Heredity is a separate hypothesis in the main theorem.
-/

namespace Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators

open GraphClasses

/-- Each component after deleting `S` contains at most two thirds of the vertices. -/
def IsBalancedSeparator {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ K : (G.induce (↑S : Set (Fin n))ᶜ).ConnectedComponent,
    3 * K.supp.ncard ≤ 2 * n

/-- A uniform separator bound sublinear in the number of edges. -/
def HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators (C : GraphClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ (b c : ℝ), 0 ≤ b ∧ b < 1 ∧ 0 < c ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ C n →
      ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), IsBalancedSeparator G S ∧
        (S.card : ℝ) ≤ c * Real.rpow ((G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) + 1) b

end Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators

concepts.title: Entropy and adjacency mass
concepts.description:
For a probability vector $\pi$ on $n$ vertices, its entropy in bits is
$$H(\pi)=-\sum_v\pi_v\log_2\pi_v,$$
with zero summands at zero probabilities. Its adjacency mass in a graph $G$ is
$$\sum_{u,v:\,uv\in E(G)}\pi_u\pi_v,$$
where ordered adjacent pairs are counted, so each edge contributes twice.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The auxiliary natural-log entropy differs by the positive factor $\ln2$.
Both definitions use mathlib's `negMulLog`, whose value at zero is zero.
The adjacency mass is an ordered sum, avoiding choices of edge orientations.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.NegMulLog
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Base
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

/-!
---
title: Entropy and adjacency mass
type: definition
---
For a probability vector $\pi$ on $n$ vertices, its entropy in bits is
$$H(\pi)=-\sum_v\pi_v\log_2\pi_v,$$
with zero summands at zero probabilities. Its adjacency mass in a graph $G$ is
$$\sum_{u,v:\,uv\in E(G)}\pi_u\pi_v,$$
where ordered adjacent pairs are counted, so each edge contributes twice.

# Formalization notes

The auxiliary natural-log entropy differs by the positive factor $\ln2$.
Both definitions use mathlib's `negMulLog`, whose value at zero is zero.
The adjacency mass is an ordered sum, avoiding choices of edge orientations.
-/

namespace Lax263307.Entropy

/-- A nonnegative vector with total mass one. -/
def IsProbability {n : ℕ} (π : Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ v, 0 ≤ π v) ∧ (∑ v, π v) = 1

/-- Entropy measured with natural logarithms. -/
noncomputable def naturalEntropy {n : ℕ} (π : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ v, Real.negMulLog (π v)

/-- Shannon entropy in bits. -/
noncomputable def entropy {n : ℕ} (π : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  naturalEntropy π / Real.log 2

/-- Total product probability of ordered adjacent vertex pairs. -/
noncomputable def adjacencyMass {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (π : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ u, ∑ v, if G.Adj u v then π u * π v else 0

/-- Sum of endpoint-cost products over unordered edges. -/
noncomputable def edgeCost {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (x : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  adjacencyMass G x / 2

end Lax263307.Entropy

concepts.title: Entropy lies between zero and the logarithm of the order
concepts.description:
For every probability vector on $n$ vertices,
$$0\le H(\pi)\le\log_2 n.$$

The upper bound follows from concavity
of $-x\log x$, with equality at the uniform distribution.

  Lax263307.Entropy.IsProbability π →

concepts.title: Edge mass bounds the average entropy decrease
concepts.description:
Let $\pi$ be a probability vector and let $q$ be a symmetric nonnegative
joint distribution with marginals $\pi$. Suppose $q_{uv}=0$ on edges of $G$.
For $\pi_v>0$, set $\pi^v_u=q_{uv}/\pi_v$. Then
$$H(\pi)-\sum_v\pi_v H(\pi^v)
  \ge\sum_{u,v:\,uv\in E(G)}\pi_u\pi_v.$$
Terms with $\pi_v=0$ have weight zero.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The lower bound uses $x\ln x\ge x-1$ on the support of $q$.
All edge pairs lie outside that support. Converting natural-log entropy
to bits only increases this nonnegative bound, since $0<\ln2\le1$.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.Entropy

/-!
---
title: Edge mass bounds the average entropy decrease
type: lemma
---
Let $\pi$ be a probability vector and let $q$ be a symmetric nonnegative
joint distribution with marginals $\pi$. Suppose $q_{uv}=0$ on edges of $G$.
For $\pi_v>0$, set $\pi^v_u=q_{uv}/\pi_v$. Then
$$H(\pi)-\sum_v\pi_v H(\pi^v)
  \ge\sum_{u,v:\,uv\in E(G)}\pi_u\pi_v.$$
Terms with $\pi_v=0$ have weight zero.

# Formalization notes

The lower bound uses $x\ln x\ge x-1$ on the support of $q$.
All edge pairs lie outside that support. Converting natural-log entropy
to bits only increases this nonnegative bound, since $0<\ln2\le1$.
-/

namespace Lax263307.EntropyGap

open Entropy

/-- The expected loss in entropy dominates the ordered adjacency mass. -/
axiom average_entropy_gap {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (π : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)
    (probability : IsProbability π) (nonnegative : ∀ u v, 0 ≤ q u v)
    (symmetric : ∀ u v, q u v = q v u)
    (marginals : ∀ v, (∑ u, q u v) = π v)
    (edge_zero : ∀ u v, G.Adj u v → q u v = 0) :
    adjacencyMass G π ≤ entropy π - ∑ v, π v * entropy (fun u => q u v / π v)

end Lax263307.EntropyGap

statements.signature:
average_entropy_gap : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj] (π : Fin n → Real) (q : Fin n → Fin n → Real),
  Lax263307.Entropy.IsProbability π →
    (∀ (u v : Fin n), Real.instLE.le 0 (q u v)) →
      (∀ (u v : Fin n), Eq (q u v) (q v u)) →
        (∀ (v : Fin n), Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun u => q u v) (π v)) →
          (∀ (u v : Fin n), G.Adj u v → Eq (q u v) 0) →
            Real.instLE.le (Lax263307.Entropy.adjacencyMass G π)
              (instHSub.hSub (Lax263307.Entropy.entropy π)
                (Finset.univ.sum fun v =>
                  instHMul.hMul (π v) (Lax263307.Entropy.entropy fun u => instHDiv.hDiv (q u v) (π v))))
statements.doc: The expected loss in entropy dominates the ordered adjacency mass.

concepts.title: Exhaustive search for small independent-set targets
concepts.description:
For a small target $k$, enumerate exactly the $k$-element vertex sets and
test independence. The first success has size exactly $k$. If the search
fails, every independent set has size less than $k$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The executable enumeration generates sublists of length $k$, without
materializing all vertex subsets. The two claims give completeness of
the candidate list and correctness of the search.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.LinearRelaxation
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Mathlib.Data.List.Sublists

/-!
---
title: Exhaustive search for small independent-set targets
type: lemma
---
For a small target $k$, enumerate exactly the $k$-element vertex sets and
test independence. The first success has size exactly $k$. If the search
fails, every independent set has size less than $k$.

# Formalization notes

The executable enumeration generates sublists of length $k$, without
materializing all vertex subsets. The two claims give completeness of
the candidate list and correctness of the search.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ExhaustiveTargets

/-- Enumerate the vertex sets of one prescribed cardinality. -/
def candidates (n k : ℕ) : List (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  ((List.finRange n).sublistsLen k).map List.toFinset

/-- Deterministic exact search at target `k`. -/
def findIndependentSet {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k : ℕ) : Option (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  (candidates n k).find? fun I => decide (G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)))

/-- Every size-`k` vertex set occurs, and no other cardinality occurs. -/
axiom candidate_complete (n k : ℕ) (I : Finset (Fin n)) :
  I ∈ candidates n k ↔ I.card = k

/-- Search success is exact; search failure excludes every larger independent set. -/
axiom search_correct {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) :
  match findIndependentSet G k with
  | some I => G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧ I.card = k
  | none => ∀ J : Finset (Fin n), G.IsIndepSet (J : Set (Fin n)) → J.card < k

end Lax263307.ExhaustiveTargets

candidate_complete : ∀ (n k : Nat) (I : Finset (Fin n)),
  Iff (List.instMembership.mem (Lax263307.ExhaustiveTargets.candidates n k) I) (Eq I.card k)
statements.doc: Every size-`k` vertex set occurs, and no other cardinality occurs.

  Lax263307.ExhaustiveTargets.search_correct.match_1 (fun x => Prop)
    (Lax263307.ExhaustiveTargets.findIndependentSet G k)
    (fun I => And (G.IsIndepSet (Finset.instSetLike.coe I)) (Eq I.card k)) fun _ =>
    ∀ (J : Finset (Fin n)), G.IsIndepSet (Finset.instSetLike.coe J) → instLTNat.lt J.card k

concepts.title: Finite product sampling and coordinate marginals
concepts.description:
Independent finite coordinates have total product mass one. Restricting to
any injectively selected coordinates recovers the product law on precisely
those coordinates. The remaining coordinates sum out to one.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.PathSampling
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Prod

/-!
---
title: Finite product sampling and coordinate marginals
type: lemma
---
Independent finite coordinates have total product mass one. Restricting to
any injectively selected coordinates recovers the product law on precisely
those coordinates. The remaining coordinates sum out to one.
-/

namespace Lax263307.FiniteProductSampling

variable {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq ι]

noncomputable def weight (f : ι → κ → ℝ) (φ : ι → κ) : ℝ := ∏ a, f a (φ a)

axiom normalized (f : ι → κ → ℝ) (mass : ∀ a, (∑ x, f a x) = 1) :
    (∑ φ : ι → κ, weight f φ) = 1

axiom embedding_marginal {k : ℕ} (f : ι → κ → ℝ)
    (mass : ∀ a, (∑ x, f a x) = 1) (j : Fin k ↪ ι) (H : (Fin k → κ) → ℝ) :
    (∑ φ : ι → κ, weight f φ * H (fun a => φ (j a))) =
      ∑ ψ : Fin k → κ, weight (fun a => f (j a)) ψ * H ψ

end Lax263307.FiniteProductSampling

statements.signature:
embedding_marginal : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : Fintype κ] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] {k : Nat}
  (f : ι → κ → Real),
  (∀ (a : ι), Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun x => f a x) 1) →
    ∀ (j : Function.Embedding (Fin k) ι) (H : (Fin k → κ) → Real),
      Eq
        (Finset.univ.sum fun φ =>
          instHMul.hMul (Lax263307.FiniteProductSampling.weight f φ)
            (H fun a => φ (Function.instFunLikeEmbedding.coe j a)))
        (Finset.univ.sum fun ψ =>
          instHMul.hMul (Lax263307.FiniteProductSampling.weight (fun a => f (Function.instFunLikeEmbedding.coe j a)) ψ)
            (H ψ))

normalized : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : Fintype κ] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (f : ι → κ → Real),
  (∀ (a : ι), Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun x => f a x) 1) →
    Eq (Finset.univ.sum fun φ => Lax263307.FiniteProductSampling.weight f φ) 1

concepts.title: The split flow-cut certificate must give a cheap separation
concepts.description:
In a hereditary class with a power bag bound, sufficiently large target and
sparsity parameters rule out the high-flow branch of the directed split
certificate. If $\gamma k\le\ell n^2$, its projected route loads would
meet the forbidden bounded-load distribution hypotheses. The returned cut
therefore projects to two nonempty covering shores with no cross edge and
separator cost at most $4\rho|A||B|/\gamma$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The shores are the actual minus/plus port projections of the certificate's
cut. This is the certificate analysis needed by the repeated-cut procedure;
the registered RAM solver and the wrapper cost are handled separately.
The main theorem derives the power bag premise from its separator hypothesis.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.NoBoundedLoadRoutes
import Lax263307.RouteDistributions
import Lax263307.VertexSplitting

/-!
---
title: The split flow-cut certificate must give a cheap separation
type: lemma
---
In a hereditary class with a power bag bound, sufficiently large target and
sparsity parameters rule out the high-flow branch of the directed split
certificate. If $\gamma k\le\ell n^2$, its projected route loads would
meet the forbidden bounded-load distribution hypotheses. The returned cut
therefore projects to two nonempty covering shores with no cross edge and
separator cost at most $4\rho|A||B|/\gamma$.

# Formalization notes

The shores are the actual minus/plus port projections of the certificate's
cut. This is the certificate analysis needed by the repeated-cut procedure;
the registered RAM solver and the wrapper cost are handled separately.
The main theorem derives the power bag premise from its separator hypothesis.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ForcedSeparation

open Entropy (edgeCost)
open Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate (Certificate)
open scoped NNReal NNRat
open GraphClasses PowerBagBounds VertexSplitting
open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

axiom certificate_separation (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (a A : ℕ) (a_positive : 0 < a) (A_positive : 0 < A) (class_bound : HasPowerBagBound C a A) :
    ∃ K : ℕ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G ∈ C n → 0 < n → ∀ (x : Fin n → ℚ≥0) (large : ℚ≥0)
      (certificate : Certificate (2 * n)) (ρ γ k p : ℝ) (ℓ : ℕ),
      0 < ℓ → 0 ≤ ρ → 0 < γ → 0 < k → 0 < p →
      γ * k ≤ (ℓ : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 → (∀ v, (x v : ℝ) ≤ 1) →
      (∑ v, (x v : ℝ)) ≤ k →
      edgeCost G (fun v => (x v : ℝ)) ≤ k ^ 2 / p →
      (K : ℝ) * ((ℓ : ℝ) + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2) ≤ k →
      (2 * K : ℝ) * ((ℓ : ℝ) + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2) ≤ p →
      AdmissibleCut (splitInstance G x large).weights certificate.cut →
      IsArcConcurrentFlow .directed (splitInstance G x large).network
        (splitInstance G x large).weights (certificate.flow.value : ℝ≥0) certificate.flow.flow →
      (ratioCost (splitInstance G x large).network (splitInstance G x large).weights certificate.cut : ℝ) ≤
        ρ * (certificate.flow.value : ℝ) →

concepts.title: Hereditary graph classes
concepts.description:
A class of finite simple graphs is hereditary if it is closed under taking
induced subgraphs and under isomorphism.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Graphs are represented on vertex sets $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Closure under
induced embeddings includes both induced subgraphs and all relabelings.
No algorithm for recognizing membership in the class is assumed.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Maps

/-!
---
title: Hereditary graph classes
type: definition
---
A class of finite simple graphs is hereditary if it is closed under taking
induced subgraphs and under isomorphism.

# Formalization notes

Graphs are represented on vertex sets $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Closure under
induced embeddings includes both induced subgraphs and all relabelings.
No algorithm for recognizing membership in the class is assumed.
-/

namespace Lax263307.GraphClasses

/-- A class of finite simple graphs, represented on numbered vertex sets. -/
abbrev GraphClass := (n : ℕ) → Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))

/-- Every graph that embeds as an induced subgraph of a member also belongs. -/
def IsHereditary (C : GraphClass) : Prop :=
  ∀ (m n : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
    G ∈ C n → Nonempty (H ↪g G) → H ∈ C m

end Lax263307.GraphClasses

concepts.title: Conditioning with a quantitative moment lower bound
concepts.description:
A high edge cost forces entropy decrease even after conditioning choices
with extremely small marginal probability are excluded. Some choice of
probability at least tau=1/(2np(log2 n+1)) decreases entropy by more than
1/p. Within r≥p(log2 n+1) steps, a sparse conditioning set is therefore
reached with raw moment at least tau^r.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
This strengthens the positive-moment existence guarantee. The quantitative
lower bound prevents a violated component inequality from having an
arbitrarily small raw gap at a feasible query. It is used by the strong-gap
ellipsoid argument; the rational search is formalized in `HeavyRationalConditioning`.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.ConditioningDistribution
import Lax263307.EntropyGap
import Lax263307.EntropyBounds
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log

/-!
---
title: Conditioning with a quantitative moment lower bound
type: lemma
---
A high edge cost forces entropy decrease even after conditioning choices
with extremely small marginal probability are excluded. Some choice of
probability at least tau=1/(2np(log2 n+1)) decreases entropy by more than
1/p. Within r≥p(log2 n+1) steps, a sparse conditioning set is therefore
reached with raw moment at least tau^r.

# Formalization notes

This strengthens the positive-moment existence guarantee. The quantitative
lower bound prevents a violated component inequality from having an
arbitrarily small raw gap at a feasible query. It is used by the strong-gap
ellipsoid argument; the rational search is formalized in `HeavyRationalConditioning`.
-/

namespace Lax263307.HeavyConditioning

open LinearRelaxation ConditioningDistribution Entropy

noncomputable def probabilityFloor (n p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  1 / (2 * (n : ℝ) * p * ((Nat.log2 n : ℝ) + 1))

axiom heavy_entropy_decrease {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k r p : ℕ) (y : MomentVector n r) (feasible : IsFeasible G k r y)
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (size : A.card < r) (positive : 0 < value y A)
    (target_positive : 0 < k) (threshold_positive : 0 < p) (order_positive : 0 < n)
    (expensive : (k : ℝ) ^ 2 / p < edgeCost G (conditioned y A)) :
    ∃ v : Fin n, probabilityFloor n p ≤ marginal y A k v ∧
      entropy (marginal y (insert v A) k) < entropy (marginal y A k) - 1 / p

axiom heavy_low_edge_cost {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k r p : ℕ) (y : MomentVector n r) (feasible : IsFeasible G k r y)
    (order_positive : 0 < n) (target_positive : 0 < k)
    (level_positive : 0 < r) (threshold_positive : 0 < p)
    (budget : (p : ℝ) * ((Nat.log2 n : ℝ) + 1) ≤ r) :
    ∃ A : Finset (Fin n), A.card ≤ r ∧ probabilityFloor n p ^ r ≤ value y A ∧
      0 < value y A ∧ (∀ v, 0 ≤ conditioned y A v ∧ conditioned y A v ≤ 1) ∧
      (∑ v, conditioned y A v) = k ∧ edgeCost G (conditioned y A) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ 2 / p

end Lax263307.HeavyConditioning

concepts.title: Exact rational search above the conditioning moment floor
concepts.description:
Search the existing bounded-size candidate list using exact rational edge
cost tests and the additional moment threshold tau^r. The strengthened
entropy argument guarantees a successful candidate. The search returns
bounded costs of total mass k, sparse edge cost, and the quantitative
conditioning moment floor, without computing entropy values.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The rational floor uses integer n,p,log2 n and has an explicit denominator.
The candidate count remains at most (r+1)(n+1)^r. These lemmas give the search function's correctness.
Its RAM implementation is verified in the proof package.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.HeavyConditioning
import Lax263307.RationalConditioning

/-!
---
title: Exact rational search above the conditioning moment floor
type: lemma
---
Search the existing bounded-size candidate list using exact rational edge
cost tests and the additional moment threshold tau^r. The strengthened
entropy argument guarantees a successful candidate. The search returns
bounded costs of total mass k, sparse edge cost, and the quantitative
conditioning moment floor, without computing entropy values.

# Formalization notes

The rational floor uses integer n,p,log2 n and has an explicit denominator.
The candidate count remains at most (r+1)(n+1)^r. These lemmas give the search function's correctness.
Its RAM implementation is verified in the proof package.
-/

namespace Lax263307.HeavyRationalConditioning

open LinearRelaxation Entropy RationalConditioning HeavyConditioning

def rationalFloor (n p : ℕ) : ℚ := 1 / (2 * (n : ℚ) * p * ((Nat.log2 n : ℚ) + 1))

def HeavyPasses {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k p : ℕ) (y : RationalVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  Passes G k p y A ∧ rationalFloor n p ^ r ≤ rationalValue y A

instance {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k p : ℕ) (y : RationalVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : Decidable (HeavyPasses G k p y A) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (Passes G k p y A ∧ rationalFloor n p ^ r ≤ rationalValue y A))

def findHeavyConditioning {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k p : ℕ) (y : RationalVector n r) : Option (Finset (Fin n)) :=
  (candidates n r).find? fun A => decide (HeavyPasses G k p y A)

axiom search_correct {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (k r p : ℕ) (y : RationalVector n r) (feasible : IsFeasible G k r (realVector y))
    (order_positive : 0 < n) (target_positive : 0 < k)
    (level_positive : 0 < r) (threshold_positive : 0 < p)
    (budget : (p : ℝ) * ((Nat.log2 n : ℝ) + 1) ≤ r) :
    ∃ A : Finset (Fin n), findHeavyConditioning G k p y = some A ∧ A.card ≤ r ∧
      probabilityFloor n p ^ r ≤ value (realVector y) A ∧ 0 < value (realVector y) A ∧
      (∀ v, 0 ≤ conditioned (realVector y) A v ∧ conditioned (realVector y) A v ≤ 1) ∧
      (∑ v, conditioned (realVector y) A v) = k ∧
      edgeCost G (conditioned (realVector y) A) ≤ (k : ℝ) ^ 2 / p

end Lax263307.HeavyRationalConditioning

  Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.IsFeasible G k r (Lax263307.RationalConditioning.realVector y) →
    instLTNat.lt 0 n →

                                1))

                                  A))

concepts.title: Recursive rounding after discarding light parts
concepts.description:
Among at most $2n$ parts, those with conditioned cost at most
$\delta k/(4n)$ have total cost at most $\delta k/2$. Independent answers
at rounded targets on all heavier parts combine into an independent set,
losing a factor of at most $1-4\delta$ per recursive level.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The size guarantee is required only on heavy parts. The returned set from
every part must be independent and contained in that part. The estimates
apply with nonnegative accuracy parameter at most $1/4$.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.StrongComponentGaps
import Lax263307.ConditionedCosts
import Lax263307.RecursiveRounding

/-!
---
title: Recursive rounding after discarding light parts
type: lemma
---
Among at most $2n$ parts, those with conditioned cost at most
$\delta k/(4n)$ have total cost at most $\delta k/2$. Independent answers
at rounded targets on all heavier parts combine into an independent set,
losing a factor of at most $1-4\delta$ per recursive level.

# Formalization notes

The size guarantee is required only on heavy parts. The returned set from
every part must be independent and contained in that part. The estimates
apply with nonnegative accuracy parameter at most $1/4$.
-/

namespace Lax263307.HeavyRecursiveRounding

open LinearRelaxation SeparatorComponents
open ComponentCutEncoding

axiom ignored_cost {n : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℝ) (δ k : ℝ)
    (hn : 0 < n) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hk : 0 ≤ k) (count : Fintype.card ι ≤ 2 * n) :
    (∑ i, if δ * k / (4 * n) < c i then 0 else c i) ≤ δ * k / 2

axiom heavy_union_size {n : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (P : Partition G S ι)
    (x : Fin n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (h : ℕ) (δ : ℝ)
    (hn : 0 < n) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (small : δ ≤ 1 / 4)
    (count : Fintype.card ι ≤ 2 * n)
    (mass : (∑ v, x v) = k) (light : ∑ v ∈ S, x v ≤ δ * k)
    (I : ι → Finset (Fin n)) (targets : ι → ℕ)
    (inside : ∀ i, I i ⊆ P.vertices i)
    (independent : ∀ i, G.IsIndepSet (I i : Set (Fin n)))
    (rounded : ∀ i, δ * k / (4 * n) < ∑ v ∈ P.vertices i, x v →
      (1 - δ) * (∑ v ∈ P.vertices i, x v) < targets i)
    (answers : ∀ i, δ * k / (4 * n) < ∑ v ∈ P.vertices i, x v →
      (1 - 4 * δ) ^ h * (targets i : ℝ) ≤ (I i).card) :
    G.IsIndepSet (combine I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
      (1 - 4 * δ) ^ (h + 1) * (k : ℝ) ≤ (combine I).card

end Lax263307.HeavyRecursiveRounding

concepts.title: Restricting an induced almost-embedding to its route union
concepts.description:
Relabel the host graph induced by the nonempty union of edge routes onto
Fin. The resulting graph embeds inducedly in the original host, has the
same induced edge count, and supports the same induced almost-embedding
with each route size preserved. Isolated source vertices may receive an
arbitrary host image because they impose no endpoint condition.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.InducedRouteEdges

/-!
---
title: Restricting an induced almost-embedding to its route union
type: lemma
---
Relabel the host graph induced by the nonempty union of edge routes onto
Fin. The resulting graph embeds inducedly in the original host, has the
same induced edge count, and supports the same induced almost-embedding
with each route size preserved. Isolated source vertices may receive an
arbitrary host image because they impose no endpoint condition.
-/

namespace Lax263307.HostRestriction

open AlmostEmbeddings InducedRouteEdges

axiom restrict_to_route_union {t n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) (induced : IsInduced E)
    (nonempty : (routeUnion E).Nonempty) :
    ∃ r, ∃ K : SimpleGraph (Fin r), ∃ _f : K ↪g G, ∃ E' : AlmostEmbedding H K,
      IsInduced E' ∧ (∀ e, (E'.route e).card = (E.route e).card) ∧
      K.edgeSet.ncard = (G.induce (↑(routeUnion E) : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard

end Lax263307.HostRestriction

  (E : Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings.AlmostEmbedding H G),
  Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings.IsInduced E →
    (Lax263307.InducedRouteEdges.routeUnion E).Nonempty →
      Exists fun r =>
        Exists fun K =>
          Exists fun _f =>
            Exists fun E' =>
              And (Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings.IsInduced E')
                (And (∀ (e : H.edgeSet.Elem), Eq (E'.route e).card (E.route e).card)
                  (Eq K.edgeSet.ncard
                    (SimpleGraph.induce (Finset.instSetLike.coe (Lax263307.InducedRouteEdges.routeUnion E))
                          G).edgeSet.ncard))

concepts.title: Independent blow-ups and projection
concepts.description:
For a graph $G$ and nonnegative integer multiplicities $t_v$, replace vertex
$v$ by an independent set of $t_v$ copies. Copies of distinct vertices are
adjacent exactly when their original vertices are adjacent. Zero multiplicities
omit vertices. Lift a vertex set by taking all of its copies; project a set
of copies by taking the vertices represented by at least one selected copy.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A copy is a pair $(v,i)$ with $0\le i<t_v$. This dependent pair type has
exactly $\sum_v t_v$ elements and admits the usual finite-type instances.
The blow-up graph is the comap of $G$ along the projection to $v$.
The cardinality approximation predicate compares the returned independent
set with every independent set in this finite graph.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Maps
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Sigma
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.BigOperators

/-!
---
title: Independent blow-ups and projection
type: definition
---
For a graph $G$ and nonnegative integer multiplicities $t_v$, replace vertex
$v$ by an independent set of $t_v$ copies. Copies of distinct vertices are
adjacent exactly when their original vertices are adjacent. Zero multiplicities
omit vertices. Lift a vertex set by taking all of its copies; project a set
of copies by taking the vertices represented by at least one selected copy.

# Formalization notes

A copy is a pair $(v,i)$ with $0\le i<t_v$. This dependent pair type has
exactly $\sum_v t_v$ elements and admits the usual finite-type instances.
The blow-up graph is the comap of $G$ along the projection to $v$.
The cardinality approximation predicate compares the returned independent
set with every independent set in this finite graph.
-/

namespace Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp

/-- The vertices of an independent blow-up, including possibly empty fibres. -/
abbrev Vertex {n : ℕ} (copies : Fin n → ℕ) := (v : Fin n) × Fin (copies v)

/-- Copies are adjacent precisely when their original vertices are adjacent. -/
def graph {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (copies : Fin n → ℕ) :
    SimpleGraph (Vertex copies) := G.comap fun v => v.1

/-- All copies of a given original vertex set. -/
def lift {n : ℕ} (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (I : Finset (Fin n)) : Finset (Vertex copies) :=
  I.sigma fun _ => Finset.univ

/-- Vertices represented by at least one selected copy. -/
def project {n : ℕ} {copies : Fin n → ℕ} (K : Finset (Vertex copies)) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  K.image fun v => v.1

/-- The usual multiplicative cardinality guarantee on the blow-up graph. -/
def IsCardinalityApproximation {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (copies : Fin n → ℕ) (δ : ℚ) (K : Finset (Vertex copies)) : Prop :=
  (graph G copies).IsIndepSet (K : Set (Vertex copies)) ∧
    ∀ J : Finset (Vertex copies), (graph G copies).IsIndepSet (J : Set (Vertex copies)) →
      (1 - δ) * (J.card : ℚ) ≤ K.card

end Lax263307.IndependentBlowUp

concepts.title: Maximum-weight independent set as an optimization problem
concepts.description:
We use the optimization-problem and approximation-scheme definitions of
lax-213208. An instance is the canonical packet containing the graph order,
its row-major adjacency matrix, and the rational vertex weights. The packet
uses the registered structural presentation of a list of natural numbers.
For precision $k>0$, the scheme receives the structural arena of $(k,x)$.

A feasible output is a zero-one membership vector of an independent set.
The objective is its total weight, with negative totals replaced by zero
to meet the archive's nonnegative-objective convention. This does not change
the optimum: the empty set is feasible and has value zero. The program
constructed below returns a set of nonnegative total weight.

The input class consists exactly of canonical packets of graphs in
$\mathcal C$, with arbitrary rational weights. No solution, separator, or
other computed advice is included in the input presentation.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.GraphClasses
import Lax263307.WeightedIndependentSet
import Lax213208.QPTAS
import Lax560851.StructuralCombinators

/-!
---
title: Maximum-weight independent set as an optimization problem
type: definition
---
We use the optimization-problem and approximation-scheme definitions of
lax-213208. An instance is the canonical packet containing the graph order,
its row-major adjacency matrix, and the rational vertex weights. The packet
uses the registered structural presentation of a list of natural numbers.
For precision $k>0$, the scheme receives the structural arena of $(k,x)$.

A feasible output is a zero-one membership vector of an independent set.
The objective is its total weight, with negative totals replaced by zero
to meet the archive's nonnegative-objective convention. This does not change
the optimum: the empty set is feasible and has value zero. The program
constructed below returns a set of nonnegative total weight.

The input class consists exactly of canonical packets of graphs in
$\mathcal C$, with arbitrary rational weights. No solution, separator, or
other computed advice is included in the input presentation.
-/

namespace Lax263307.IndependentSetProblem

open GraphClasses WeightedIndependentSet
open Lax213208.OptimizationProblem
open Lax560851.StructuralPresentation Lax560851.StructuralCombinators

/-- Graph and weights, without the separately supplied accuracy parameter. -/
noncomputable abbrev encodeInstance {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (w : Fin n → ℚ) : List ℕ := by
  classical
  exact [n] ++ (List.ofFn fun u => List.ofFn fun v =>
    if G.Adj u v then 1 else 0).flatten ++
    (List.ofFn w).flatMap encodeRational

abbrev order (x : List ℕ) : ℕ := x.headD 0

/-- Interpret the matrix; symmetry and the absent diagonal are explicit. -/
def graph (x : List ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Fin (order x)) where
  Adj u v := u ≠ v ∧ x.getD (1 + u.val * order x + v.val) 0 ≠ 0 ∧
    x.getD (1 + v.val * order x + u.val) 0 ≠ 0
  symm := ⟨by rintro u v ⟨hne, huv, hvu⟩; exact ⟨Ne.symm hne, hvu, huv⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨by intro u h; exact h.1 rfl⟩

instance (x : List ℕ) : DecidableRel (graph x).Adj := fun _ _ =>
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ≠ _ ∧ _ ≠ 0 ∧ _ ≠ 0))

def weights (x : List ℕ) (v : Fin (order x)) : ℚ :=
  let offset := 1 + order x * order x + 3 * v.val
  let numerator : ℚ := x.getD (offset + 1) 0
  let denominator : ℚ := x.getD (offset + 2) 0
  (if x.getD offset 0 = 0 then numerator else -numerator) / denominator

def selected (x y : List ℕ) : Finset (Fin (order x)) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun v => y.getD v.val 0 = 1

def feasible (x y : List ℕ) : Prop :=
  y.length = order x ∧ (∀ b ∈ y, b = 0 ∨ b = 1) ∧
    (graph x).IsIndepSet (selected x y : Set (Fin (order x)))

def value (x y : List ℕ) : NNReal :=
  Real.toNNReal (weight (weights x) (selected x y))

/-- The standard structural-list presentation is injective by its constructors.
This proof is axiom-free so it can be used inside a concept definition. -/
private theorem input_faithful : (list nat).Faithful := by
  intro x y h
  change listToRaw nat x = listToRaw nat y at h
  induction x generalizing y with
  | nil => cases y <;> cases h; rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    cases y with
    | nil => cases h
    | cons y ys =>
      change Lax560851.StructuralPresentation.Raw.pair (.nat x) (listToRaw nat xs) =
        Lax560851.StructuralPresentation.Raw.pair (.nat y) (listToRaw nat ys) at h
      obtain ⟨hx, ht⟩ := Lax560851.StructuralPresentation.Raw.pair.inj h
      exact congrArg₂ List.cons (Lax560851.StructuralPresentation.Raw.nat.inj hx) (ih ht)

def problem : Problem (List ℕ) (List ℕ) where
  direction := .maximize
  feasible := feasible
  value := value
  input := list nat
  output := id
  input_faithful := input_faithful
  output_injective := fun _ _ h => h

def instances (C : GraphClass) : Set (List ℕ) :=
  {x | ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (w : Fin n → ℚ),
    G ∈ C n ∧ x = encodeInstance G w}

end Lax263307.IndependentSetProblem

concepts.title: A class width bound obstructs induced route sampling
concepts.description:
Suppose every graph in a hereditary class has a decomposition whose bag
size is bounded by a monotone function $W$ of its edge count. An induced
almost-embedding of a source graph of maximum degree $d$, with routes of
size at most $L$, transfers this to source bags of size at most
$\max\{1,2dW(d|E(H)|L^2)\}$.

Discarding long routes adds at most their number to this bound on treewidth
plus one. A good sample with total size at most $4M$ therefore gives a
number $q$ of discarded edges with $Lq\le4M$ and the resulting source
width bound. This is the quantitative obstruction used with a source
family of linear treewidth.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The monotone class bag bound is an explicit hypothesis here. The main theorem derives it
from its separator hypothesis.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.HostRestriction
import Lax263307.IsolatedEmbeddingTransfer
import Lax263307.GraphClasses
import Lax263307.RoutePruning
import Lax263307.SampledAlmostEmbeddings

/-!
---
title: A class width bound obstructs induced route sampling
type: lemma
---
Suppose every graph in a hereditary class has a decomposition whose bag
size is bounded by a monotone function $W$ of its edge count. An induced
almost-embedding of a source graph of maximum degree $d$, with routes of
size at most $L$, transfers this to source bags of size at most
$\max\{1,2dW(d|E(H)|L^2)\}$.

Discarding long routes adds at most their number to this bound on treewidth
plus one. A good sample with total size at most $4M$ therefore gives a
number $q$ of discarded edges with $Lq\le4M$ and the resulting source
width bound. This is the quantitative obstruction used with a source
family of linear treewidth.

# Formalization notes

The monotone class bag bound is an explicit hypothesis here. The main theorem derives it
from its separator hypothesis.
-/

namespace Lax263307.InducedEmbeddingWidth

open PathSampling (adjacencyProbability collisionProbability expectedSize)
open RouteDistributions (Distribution)
open RoutePruning (longEdges)
open AlmostEmbeddings InducedRouteEdges Lax228581.Treewidth
open GraphClasses

def HasBagBound (C : GraphClass) (W : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∈ C n →
    ∃ D : TreeDecomposition G, ∀ i, (D.bag i).card ≤ W G.edgeSet.ncard

axiom transfer_class_bound {t n : ℕ} (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (W : ℕ → ℕ) (monotone : Monotone W) (class_bound : HasBagBound C W)
    (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (member : G ∈ C n) (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) (induced : IsInduced E) (d L : ℕ)
    (degree_bound : ∀ v, H.degree v ≤ d) (length_bound : ∀ e, (E.route e).card ≤ L) :
    ∃ D : TreeDecomposition H, ∀ i, (D.bag i).card ≤
      max 1 (2 * d * W (d * H.edgeSet.ncard * L ^ 2))

axiom treewidth_after_pruning {t n : ℕ} (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (W : ℕ → ℕ) (monotone : Monotone W) (class_bound : HasBagBound C W)
    (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (member : G ∈ C n) (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) (induced : IsInduced E) (d L : ℕ)
    (degree_bound : ∀ v, H.degree v ≤ d) :
    treewidth H + 1 ≤ max 1 (2 * d * W (d * H.edgeSet.ncard * L ^ 2)) +
      (longEdges E L).card

axiom sampled_width_bound {t n q : ℕ} (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (W : ℕ → ℕ) (monotone : Monotone W) (class_bound : HasBagBound C W)
    (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (member : G ∈ C n) (D : Distribution G q) (hn : 0 < n)
    (d L : ℕ) (degree_bound : ∀ v, H.degree v ≤ d) (M : ℝ) (positive : 0 < M)
    (bad_budget : (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) ^ 2 * (collisionProbability D.toSampling +
      adjacencyProbability G D.toSampling) ≤ 1 / 4)
    (length_budget : (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) * expectedSize D.toSampling ≤ M) :
    ∃ removed : ℕ, (L : ℝ) * removed ≤ 4 * M ∧
      treewidth H + 1 ≤ max 1 (2 * d * W (d * H.edgeSet.ncard * L ^ 2)) + removed

end Lax263307.InducedEmbeddingWidth

  Lax263307.GraphClasses.IsHereditary C →
    ∀ (W : Nat → Nat),
      Monotone W →
        Lax263307.InducedEmbeddingWidth.HasBagBound C W →
          ∀ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [inst : DecidableRel H.Adj] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
            Set.instMembership.mem (C n) G →
              ∀ (E : Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings.AlmostEmbedding H G),

    ∀ (W : Nat → Nat),
      Monotone W →
        Lax263307.InducedEmbeddingWidth.HasBagBound C W →
          ∀ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [inst : DecidableRel H.Adj] (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
            Set.instMembership.mem (C n) G →
              ∀ (E : Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings.AlmostEmbedding H G),

concepts.title: Few edges in the graph induced by short routes
concepts.description:
Suppose an induced almost-embedding of a graph $H$ of maximum degree at most
$d$ uses at most $L$ host vertices per route. The union of its routes has
at most $|E(H)|L$ vertices. Its induced graph has maximum degree at most
$2dL$, and therefore at most $d|E(H)|L^2$ edges.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.DegreeSum

/-!
---
title: Few edges in the graph induced by short routes
type: lemma
---
Suppose an induced almost-embedding of a graph $H$ of maximum degree at most
$d$ uses at most $L$ host vertices per route. The union of its routes has
at most $|E(H)|L$ vertices. Its induced graph has maximum degree at most
$2dL$, and therefore at most $d|E(H)|L^2$ edges.
-/

namespace Lax263307.InducedRouteEdges

open AlmostEmbeddings

/-- All host vertices used by some edge route. -/
noncomputable def routeUnion {t n : ℕ} {H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)}
    [DecidableRel H.Adj] {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)} (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) : Finset (Fin n) := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.biUnion E.route

/-- Bounded-length induced routes induce few host edges. -/
axiom edge_bound {t n : ℕ} (H : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (E : AlmostEmbedding H G) (d L : ℕ)
    (induced : IsInduced E) (degree_bound : ∀ v, H.degree v ≤ d)
    (length_bound : ∀ e, (E.route e).card ≤ L) :
    (G.induce (↑(routeUnion E) : Set (Fin n))).edgeSet.ncard ≤
      d * H.edgeSet.ncard * L ^ 2

end Lax263307.InducedRouteEdges

  Lax263307.AlmostEmbeddings.IsInduced E →
    (∀ (v : Fin t), instLENat.le (H.degree v) d) →

          (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul d H.edgeSet.ncard) (instHPow.hPow L 2))

concepts.title: Almost-embedding transfer with isolated source vertices
concepts.description:
An almost-embedding of a graph of maximum degree at most $d$ transfers a
host decomposition with bag size at most $w$ to source bags of size at most
$\max\{1,2dw\}$, even if the source has isolated vertices. Restrict to
its nonisolated vertices, apply the connected-carrier transfer, then attach
a singleton leaf bag for each omitted isolated vertex.

concepts.title: The independent-set relaxation and its exact hull
concepts.description:
For an $n$-vertex graph $G$, target $k$, and level $r$, the relaxation
$R_r(G,k)$ has coordinates $y_A$ for vertex sets $|A|\le r+2$ and constraints
$$y_\varnothing=1,\qquad 0\le y_A\le1,$$
$$y_{A\cup\{v\}}\le y_A\quad (|A|\le r+1),$$
$$y_A=0\quad\text{if }A\text{ is not independent},$$
$$\sum_v y_{A\cup\{v\}}=k y_A\quad (|A|\le r+1).$$
The exact hull $P_r(G,k)$ is the convex hull of the vectors
$y_A=\mathbf1[A\subseteq I]$ over independent sets $I$ of size $k$.
For $y_A>0$, conditioning on $A$ gives costs $x_v=y_{A\cup\{v\}}/y_A$.

sections.title: Formalization notes

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Hull
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

/-!
---
title: The independent-set relaxation and its exact hull
type: definition
---
For an $n$-vertex graph $G$, target $k$, and level $r$, the relaxation
$R_r(G,k)$ has coordinates $y_A$ for vertex sets $|A|\le r+2$ and constraints
$$y_\varnothing=1,\qquad 0\le y_A\le1,$$
$$y_{A\cup\{v\}}\le y_A\quad (|A|\le r+1),$$
$$y_A=0\quad\text{if }A\text{ is not independent},$$
$$\sum_v y_{A\cup\{v\}}=k y_A\quad (|A|\le r+1).$$
The exact hull $P_r(G,k)$ is the convex hull of the vectors
$y_A=\mathbf1[A\subseteq I]$ over independent sets $I$ of size $k$.
For $y_A>0$, conditioning on $A$ gives costs $x_v=y_{A\cup\{v\}}/y_A$.

# Formalization notes

The coordinate type contains exactly the sets of size at most $r+2$;
there are no coordinates for larger sets. The accessor is extended by zero
outside this domain, solely to simplify notation. Every constraint that
uses it supplies a size bound ensuring that it reads an actual coordinate.
The vector space and convex hull are over the reals, as in the paper;
the algorithms will use rational points in this space.
-/

namespace Lax263307.LinearRelaxation

/-- The coordinate sets of the level-`r` relaxation. -/
abbrev Coordinate (n r : ℕ) := {A : Finset (Fin n) // A.card ≤ r + 2}

/-- A vector with precisely the coordinates used by the relaxation. -/
abbrev MomentVector (n r : ℕ) := Coordinate n r → ℝ

/-- Read a coordinate, returning zero outside the truncated coordinate domain. -/
def value {n r : ℕ} (y : MomentVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ :=
  if h : A.card ≤ r + 2 then y ⟨A, h⟩ else 0

/-- The indicator encoding of a vertex set. -/
def indicator {n : ℕ} (r : ℕ) (I : Finset (Fin n)) : MomentVector n r :=
  fun A => if A.val ⊆ I then 1 else 0

/-- The five families of linear constraints defining `R_r(G,k)`. -/
structure IsFeasible {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k r : ℕ)
    (y : MomentVector n r) : Prop where
  /-- The empty moment is normalized. -/
  normalized : value y ∅ = 1
  /-- Each moment lies in the unit interval. -/
  bounds : ∀ A, 0 ≤ y A ∧ y A ≤ 1
  /-- Adding a vertex cannot increase a moment. -/
  monotone : ∀ A : Finset (Fin n), A.card ≤ r + 1 →
    ∀ v, value y (insert v A) ≤ value y A
  /-- Nonindependent sets have zero moment. -/
  vanishes : ∀ A : Coordinate n r, ¬G.IsIndepSet (A.val : Set (Fin n)) → y A = 0
  /-- The cardinality constraint remains valid after conditioning. -/
  mass : ∀ A : Finset (Fin n), A.card ≤ r + 1 →
    ∑ v : Fin n, value y (insert v A) = (k : ℝ) * value y A

/-- The convex hull of encodings of size-`k` independent sets. -/
def independentSetHull {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k r : ℕ) :
    Set (MomentVector n r) :=
  convexHull ℝ {y | ∃ I : Finset (Fin n),
    G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧ I.card = k ∧ y = indicator r I}

/-- Vertex costs after conditioning on inclusion of `A`. -/
noncomputable def conditioned {n r : ℕ} (y : MomentVector n r)
    (A : Finset (Fin n)) (v : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  value y (insert v A) / value y A

/-- A certified upper bound on independent sets contained in a vertex set. -/
def IsIndependenceBound {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (C : Finset (Fin n)) (u : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ J : Finset (Fin n), J ⊆ C → G.IsIndepSet (J : Set (Fin n)) → J.card ≤ u

end Lax263307.LinearRelaxation

concepts.title: QPTAS for maximum-weight independent set
concepts.description:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a hereditary graph class with strongly edge-sublinear
separators. Then maximum-weight independent set admits a deterministic
quasipolynomial-time approximation scheme on $\mathcal C$.

For every $G\in\mathcal C$ and integer precision $k>0$, one fixed program
computes an independent set of weight at least $\alpha_w(G)/(1+1/k)$.
Its running time, for each fixed $k$, is quasipolynomial in the binary size
of the structurally encoded graph and rational weights, as specified by
the registered `QPTAS` definition in lax-213208.
No separator or algorithm for finding one is part of the input.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The conclusion `HasQPTAS C` specializes lax-213208's `QPTAS` to the MWIS
problem. The structured algorithm uses accuracy $\varepsilon=1/(k+1)$;
its checked source bound is
$$\exp\!\left((\varepsilon^{-1}\log(n+2))^{O_{\mathcal C}(1)}\right)
  +(\ell+1)^{O_{\mathcal C}(1)},$$
where $\ell$ measures the rational parameters. The proof absorbs the structural
reader and compiler costs into the archive's quasipolynomial envelope, and
uses lax-62's high-level compilation theorem directly. The separator hypothesis
uses the $m+1$ normalization explained in `EdgeSublinearSeparators`.

import Lax263307.EdgeSublinearSeparators
import Lax263307.QPTAS

/-!

title: QPTAS for maximum-weight independent set
type: theorem
---

Its running time, for each fixed $k$, is quasipolynomial in the binary size
of the structurally encoded graph and rational weights, as specified by
the registered `QPTAS` definition in lax-213208.
No separator or algorithm for finding one is part of the input.

# Formalization notes

The conclusion `HasQPTAS C` specializes lax-213208's `QPTAS` to the MWIS
problem. The structured algorithm uses accuracy $\varepsilon=1/(k+1)$;
its checked source bound is
$$\exp\!\left((\varepsilon^{-1}\log(n+2))^{O_{\mathcal C}(1)}\right)

where $\ell$ measures the rational parameters. The proof absorbs the structural

namespace Lax263307.MainTheorem

open GraphClasses EdgeSublinearSeparators QPTAS

/-- Theorem 2: the deterministic weighted approximation scheme. -/
axiom exists_qptas (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (separators : HasStronglyEdgeSublinearSeparators C) : HasQPTAS C

concepts.title: The moment relaxation as an explicit rational linear program
concepts.description:
Use the computable moment catalog as the LP variable order. Paired
normalization rows, upper-bound rows, nonindependence rows, insertion
monotonicity rows, and paired conditioned-mass rows encode the relaxation
exactly. Primal nonnegativity supplies the coordinate lower bounds.
The resulting rational LP has N variables and 2+4N+Nn rows, where
N≤(r+3)(n+1)^(r+2).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
All finite index concatenations and graph independence tests are computable.
Rows indexed by sets of size r+2 are inactive in the two families restricted
to size at most r+1. Collected component-cut coefficients can use the same
catalog order, with evaluation exactly equal to a native finite dot product.
Dense input construction and solver execution on RAM remain separate bounds.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.CoordinateCatalog
import Lax263307.ComponentCutEncoding
import Lax109476.RationalCertificates

/-!
---
title: The moment relaxation as an explicit rational linear program
type: lemma
---
Use the computable moment catalog as the LP variable order. Paired
normalization rows, upper-bound rows, nonindependence rows, insertion
monotonicity rows, and paired conditioned-mass rows encode the relaxation
exactly. Primal nonnegativity supplies the coordinate lower bounds.
The resulting rational LP has N variables and 2+4N+Nn rows, where
N≤(r+3)(n+1)^(r+2).

# Formalization notes

All finite index concatenations and graph independence tests are computable.
Rows indexed by sets of size r+2 are inactive in the two families restricted
to size at most r+1. Collected component-cut coefficients can use the same
catalog order, with evaluation exactly equal to a native finite dot product.
Dense input construction and solver execution on RAM remain separate bounds.
-/

namespace Lax263307.MomentLP

open ComponentCutEncoding (evaluate)
open LinearRelaxation CoordinateCatalog
open Lax109476.LinearProgram Lax109476.RationalCertificates

abbrev dimension (n r : ℕ) : ℕ := (catalog n r).length
abbrev Index (n r : ℕ) := Fin (dimension n r)

def decode {K : Type} {n r : ℕ} (x : Index n r → K) : Coordinate n r → K :=
  fun A => x ((indexing n r).symm A)

def encode {K : Type} {n r : ℕ} (y : Coordinate n r → K) : Index n r → K :=
  fun j => y (indexing n r j)

def singleRow {n r : ℕ} (A : Finset (Fin n)) (j : Index n r) : ℚ :=
  if A = (indexing n r j).val then 1 else 0

def monotoneRow {n r : ℕ} (A : Finset (Fin n)) (v : Fin n) (j : Index n r) : ℚ :=
  singleRow (insert v A) j - singleRow A j

def massRow {n r : ℕ} (A : Finset (Fin n)) (k : ℕ) (j : Index n r) : ℚ :=
  (∑ v, singleRow (insert v A) j) - (k : ℚ) * singleRow A j

def program {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k r : ℕ) :
    Program ℚ (2 + (dimension n r + (dimension n r + (dimension n r * n + (dimension n r + dimension n r))))) (dimension n r) where
  A := Fin.addCases
    (fun i : Fin 2 => fun j => if i = 0 then singleRow ∅ j else -singleRow ∅ j)
    (Fin.addCases
      (fun i : Index n r => singleRow (indexing n r i).val)
      (Fin.addCases
        (fun i : Index n r => fun j =>
          if G.IsIndepSet ((indexing n r i).val : Set (Fin n)) then 0 else singleRow (indexing n r i).val j)
        (Fin.addCases
          (fun i : Fin (dimension n r * n) =>
            let uv := finProdFinEquiv.symm i
            if (indexing n r uv.1).val.card ≤ r + 1 then monotoneRow (indexing n r uv.1).val uv.2 else fun _ => 0)
          (Fin.addCases
            (fun i : Index n r =>
              if (indexing n r i).val.card ≤ r + 1 then massRow (indexing n r i).val k else fun _ => 0)
            (fun i : Index n r => fun j =>
              if (indexing n r i).val.card ≤ r + 1 then -massRow (indexing n r i).val k j else 0)))))
  b := Fin.addCases (fun i : Fin 2 => if i = 0 then 1 else -1)
    (Fin.addCases (fun _ : Index n r => 1) (fun _ => 0))
  c := fun _ => 0

axiom decode_encode {K : Type} {n r : ℕ} (y : Coordinate n r → K) : decode (encode y) = y

axiom single_row_value {n r : ℕ} (x : Index n r → ℝ) (A : Finset (Fin n)) :
    (∑ j, (singleRow A j : ℝ) * x j) = value (decode x) A

axiom primal_characterization {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k r : ℕ)
    (x : Index n r → ℝ) :
    PrimalFeasible (toReal (program G k r)) x ↔ IsFeasible G k r (decode x)

axiom evaluate_encoding {n r : ℕ} (a : Coordinate n r → ℤ) (x : Index n r → ℝ) :
    evaluate a (decode x) =
      (fun j => ((encode a j : ℤ) : ℝ)) ⬝ᵥ x

end Lax263307.MomentLP

    (Lax263307.LinearRelaxation.value (Lax263307.MomentLP.decode x) A)

concepts.title: Encoding the moment-coordinate catalogue
concepts.description:
The moment-coordinate catalogue lists subsets of the vertex set in the
order used by the relaxation. Each subset is represented by its binary
membership mask; `words` is the resulting list of masks.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Masks encode subsets of `Fin n`. The catalogue contains only the subsets
needed by the relaxation, rather than an array indexed by all $2^n$ masks.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.CoordinateCatalog
import Lax808846.Ram
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Colex

/-!
---
title: Encoding the moment-coordinate catalogue
type: definition
---
The moment-coordinate catalogue lists subsets of the vertex set in the
order used by the relaxation. Each subset is represented by its binary
membership mask; `words` is the resulting list of masks.

# Formalization notes

Masks encode subsets of `Fin n`. The catalogue contains only the subsets
needed by the relaxation, rather than an array indexed by all $2^n$ masks.
-/

namespace Lax263307.NativeCatalog

open CoordinateCatalog (catalog)
def subsetMask {n : ℕ} (I : Finset (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  Finset.equivBitIndices.symm (I.image Fin.val)

def words (n r : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  (catalog n r).map (fun A => subsetMask A.val)

end Lax263307.NativeCatalog

concepts.title: Input encoding for the moment linear program
concepts.description:
The input to the moment-LP constructor records the graph order, the
independent-set target, the relaxation level, and the adjacency matrix.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The first four words are $n$, $k$, $r$, and $n^2$. They are followed by the
adjacency bits in row-major order. This encoding is used by the concrete
RAM constructor in the proof package.

concepts.title: A uniform RAM program for the rounded ellipsoid update
concepts.description:
One fixed finite RAM program reads a rational shape, an integer cut normal,
a rational center, and the iteration index, and writes the rounded next
shape and center. Both its instruction count and sufficient word length
are polynomial in the dimension, iteration index, and coordinate bit bound.
It works at every larger word length. The input has no length prefix.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
This statement concerns actual `Lax808846.Ram.RunsTo`. The proof compiles
the registered LP submission's complete rational ellipsoid update, adding
the input reader and canonical output writer. It is one subroutine of the
recursive QPTAS; it does not assert that the complete QPTAS program exists.

import Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch
import Lax808846.Ram

/-!
---
title: A uniform RAM program for the rounded ellipsoid update
type: lemma
---
One fixed finite RAM program reads a rational shape, an integer cut normal,
a rational center, and the iteration index, and writes the rounded next
shape and center. Both its instruction count and sufficient word length
are polynomial in the dimension, iteration index, and coordinate bit bound.
It works at every larger word length. The input has no length prefix.

# Formalization notes

This statement concerns actual `Lax808846.Ram.RunsTo`. The proof compiles
the registered LP submission's complete rational ellipsoid update, adding
the input reader and canonical output writer. It is one subroutine of the
recursive QPTAS; it does not assert that the complete QPTAS program exists.
-/

namespace Lax263307.NativeRoundedStep

open Lax808846.Ram (Program RunsTo)
open Matrix RoundedOracleSearch Lax109476.RationalEncoding

def height (q : ℚ) (h : ℕ) : Prop := q.num.natAbs ≤ 2 ^ h ∧ q.den ≤ 2 ^ h

def encodeInput {n : ℕ} (k : ℕ) (state : State n) (a : Fin n → ℤ) : List ℕ :=
  [n, k] ++ (List.ofFn fun i => encodeVector (state.1 i)).flatten ++
    encodeVector (rationalNormal a) ++ encodeVector state.2

def encodeOutput {n : ℕ} (state : State n) : List ℕ :=
  (List.ofFn fun i : Fin (n * n) => state.1 i.divNat i.modNat).flatMap encodeRational ++
    encodeVector state.2

axiom exists_program : ∃ p : Program, ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧
    ∀ (n k h : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → 1 ≤ h →
      ∀ (state : State n) (a : Fin n → ℤ),
        (∀ i j, height (state.1 i j) h) →
        (∀ i, height (rationalNormal a i) h) → (∀ i, height (state.2 i) h) →
        0 < rationalNormal a ⬝ᵥ (state.1 *ᵥ rationalNormal a) →
        ∀ w : ℕ, c * (n + h + k + 1) ^ 12 ≤ w →
          ∃ t ≤ c * (n + h + k + 1) ^ 12, RunsTo w p
            (encodeInput k state a) (encodeOutput (update k state a)) t

end Lax263307.NativeRoundedStep

                  (∀ (i : Fin n), Lax263307.NativeRoundedStep.height (state.snd i) h) →

                        (dotProduct (Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch.rationalNormal a)
                          (state.fst.mulVec (Lax263307.RoundedOracleSearch.rationalNormal a))) →

                        instLENat.le

concepts.title: The recursive oracle near the moment relaxation
concepts.description:
The oracle searches for a heavy conditioning set, computes separators,
and queries the resulting parts. Its possible outputs are an independent
set, a component cut, or rejection.

The correctness predicate requires an approximation guarantee for a found
set and a valid inequality with a quantitative gap for a returned cut.
It rules out rejection under the oracle's hypotheses.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
`ChildCorrect` specifies the recursive answers on balanced parts.
`Correct` specifies the corresponding answer or cut at the current level.
The function itself is computable for the supplied flow solver and child
queries.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.ComputedSeparators
import Lax263307.ComputedRounding
import Lax263307.HeavyRationalConditioning
import Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters

/-!
---
title: The recursive oracle near the moment relaxation
type: definition
---
The oracle searches for a heavy conditioning set, computes separators,
and queries the resulting parts. Its possible outputs are an independent
set, a component cut, or rejection.

The correctness predicate requires an approximation guarantee for a found
set and a valid inequality with a quantitative gap for a returned cut.
It rules out rejection under the oracle's hypotheses.

# Formalization notes

`ChildCorrect` specifies the recursive answers on balanced parts.
`Correct` specifies the corresponding answer or cut at the current level.
The function itself is computable for the supplied flow solver and child
queries.
-/

namespace Lax263307.NearOracle

open AlgorithmParameters (level load sparsity)
open ComponentCutEncoding (coefficient evaluate)
open ComputedRounding (collect)
open ComputedSeparators (cuts pieces step)
open HeavyRationalConditioning (findHeavyConditioning)
open scoped NNRat
open LinearRelaxation RationalConditioning

def costs {n r : ℕ} (y : RationalVector n r) (A : Finset (Fin n)) (v : Fin n) : ℚ≥0 :=
  ⟨max 0 (rationalValue y (insert v A) / rationalValue y A), le_max_left _ _⟩

def order (q : ℕ) : List (Option (Fin q)) := none :: (List.finRange q).map some

inductive Result (n : ℕ)
  | found (vertices : Finset (Fin n))
  | cut (conditioning vertices : Finset (Fin n)) (bound : ℕ)
  | reject

def run {n : ℕ} (flow : List ℕ → List ℕ) (a K B D : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ)
    (y : RationalVector n (level a K B n D))
    (child : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))) : Result n :=
  let p := sparsity a K B n D
  match findHeavyConditioning G k p y with
  | none => .reject
  | some A =>
    let x := costs y A
    let cs := cuts
      (step flow G x B (load B n D) k) n Finset.univ
    let parts := pieces cs
    let c : Option (Fin cs.length) → ℚ := fun i => ∑ v ∈ parts i, (x v : ℚ)
    match collect (order cs.length) parts (1 / D) k c
      (fun i t => child (parts i) t) with
    | .found I => .found I
    | .cut C u => .cut A C u

def ChildCorrect {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (D h : ℕ)
    (child : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Option (Finset (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : Finset (Fin n), 3 * C.card ≤ 2 * n → ∀ t : ℕ,
    match child C t with
    | some I => I ⊆ C ∧ G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
        (1 - 4 * (1 / (D : ℝ))) ^ h * (t : ℝ) ≤ I.card
    | none => IsIndependenceBound G C (t - 1)

def Correct {n r : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (k h D : ℕ) (η : ℝ)
    (x : MomentVector n r) : Result n → Prop
  | .found I => G.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Fin n)) ∧
      (1 - 4 * (1 / (D : ℝ))) ^ (h + 1) * (k : ℝ) ≤ I.card
  | .cut A C u => A.card ≤ r ∧ u ≤ n ∧ IsIndependenceBound G C u ∧
      (∀ z ∈ independentSetHull G k r,
        evaluate (coefficient A C u) z ≤ 0) ∧
      η * (1 / (D : ℝ)) ^ 2 / (16 * n) ≤
        evaluate (coefficient A C u) x ∧
      (∑ T : Coordinate n r, |(coefficient A C u T : ℝ)|) ≤ 2 * n
  | .reject => False

end Lax263307.NearOracle

concepts.title: Sparse bounded-load route distributions are impossible
concepts.description:
Suppose a hereditary class has a uniform power bound on decomposition bags.
There is a fixed positive integer $K$ such that a class member cannot support
a uniform-endpoint route distribution with vertex loads at most
$\ell x_v/k$, costs in $[0,1]$ of total mass at most $k$, and edge cost at
most $k^2/p$, when $k\ge K(\ell+1)^{4a+2}$ and
$p\ge2K(\ell+1)^{4a+2}$.

The registered source family supplies a graph large enough to contradict
the sampled width upper bound, while its size overshoot keeps its edge count
within the probability budgets.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The power bag bound is an explicit hypothesis. The main theorem derives it
from strongly edge-sublinear separators. No source
graph construction is needed by the separator algorithm: this family is
used only in the contradiction that rules out its high-flow branch.

import Lax263307.CostSamplingObstruction

/-!

title: Sparse bounded-load route distributions are impossible
type: lemma
---
Suppose a hereditary class has a uniform power bound on decomposition bags.
There is a fixed positive integer $K$ such that a class member cannot support
a uniform-endpoint route distribution with vertex loads at most
$\ell x_v/k$, costs in $[0,1]$ of total mass at most $k$, and edge cost at
most $k^2/p$, when $k\ge K(\ell+1)^{4a+2}$ and
$p\ge2K(\ell+1)^{4a+2}$.

The registered source family supplies a graph large enough to contradict
the sampled width upper bound, while its size overshoot keeps its edge count
within the probability budgets.

# Formalization notes

The power bag bound is an explicit hypothesis. The main theorem derives it
from strongly edge-sublinear separators. No source
graph construction is needed by the separator algorithm: this family is
used only in the contradiction that rules out its high-flow branch.
-/

namespace Lax263307.NoBoundedLoadRoutes

open Entropy (edgeCost)
open PathSampling (load)
open RouteDistributions (Distribution)
open GraphClasses PowerBagBounds Lax228581.Treewidth

axiom no_bounded_load_routes (C : GraphClass) (hereditary : IsHereditary C)
    (a A : ℕ) (a_positive : 0 < a) (A_positive : 0 < A) (class_bound : HasPowerBagBound C a A) :
    ∃ K : ℕ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ (n q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      G ∈ C n → ∀ (D : Distribution G q), 0 < n →
      ∀ (ℓ : ℕ), 0 < ℓ → ∀ (x : Fin n → ℝ) (k p : ℝ), 0 < k → 0 < p →
      (∀ v, 0 ≤ x v ∧ x v ≤ 1) → (∑ v, x v) ≤ k →
      (∀ v, load D.toSampling v ≤ (ℓ : ℝ) * x v / k) →
      edgeCost G x ≤ k ^ 2 / p →
      (K : ℝ) * ((ℓ : ℝ) + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2) ≤ k →
      (2 * K : ℝ) * ((ℓ : ℝ) + 1) ^ (4 * a + 2) ≤ p → False

end Lax263307.NoBoundedLoadRoutes

                                      (∀ (v : Fin n),
                                          Real.instLE.le (Lax263307.PathSampling.load D.toSampling v)
                                            (instHDiv.hDiv (instHMul.hMul ℓ.cast (x v)) k)) →
                                        Real.instLE.le (Lax263307.Entropy.edgeCost G x)
                                            (instHDiv.hDiv (instHPow.hPow k 2) p) →
                                          Real.instLE.le
                                              (instHMul.hMul K.cast
                                                (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd ℓ.cast 1)
                                                  (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 4 a) 2)))
                                              k →

concepts.title: Quasipolynomial bounds for the computed algorithm budgets
concepts.description:
For fixed class constants, the graph order, accuracy denominator, load,
edge sparsity, conditioning level, moment dimension, protected-radius
precision, ellipsoid iteration count, and small-target enumeration bound
all fit one quasipolynomial bound in D times the binary-logarithm scale.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The proof supplies fixed positive natural constants before n and D.
It bounds the actual integer formulas used by the algorithm, including
its conservative precision choice. The proof of the main theorem combines
these estimates with polynomial local work and logarithmic recursion to
bound the complete RAM execution.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters

/-!
---
title: Quasipolynomial bounds for the computed algorithm budgets
type: lemma
---
For fixed class constants, the graph order, accuracy denominator, load,
edge sparsity, conditioning level, moment dimension, protected-radius
precision, ellipsoid iteration count, and small-target enumeration bound
all fit one quasipolynomial bound in D times the binary-logarithm scale.

# Formalization notes

The proof supplies fixed positive natural constants before n and D.
It bounds the actual integer formulas used by the algorithm, including
its conservative precision choice. The proof of the main theorem combines
these estimates with polynomial local work and logarithmic recursion to
bound the complete RAM execution.
-/

namespace Lax263307.ParameterResources

open MomentLP (dimension)
open AlgorithmParameters

def resource (a K B n D : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  n + D + load B n D + sparsity a K B n D + level a K B n D +
    dimension n (level a K B n D) + radiusDenominator a K B n D +
    precision a K B n D + iterations a K B n D + (n + 1) ^ cutoff a K B n D

axiom resource_bound (a K B : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) :
    ∃ C d : ℕ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < d ∧ ∀ n D : ℕ, 0 < n → 0 < D →
      resource a K B n D ≤ 2 ^ (C * (D * logarithm n) ^ d)

end Lax263307.ParameterResources

  instLTNat.lt 0 K →
    Exists fun C =>
      Exists fun d =>
        And (instLTNat.lt 0 C)
          (And (instLTNat.lt 0 d)
            (∀ (n D : Nat),
              instLTNat.lt 0 n →
                instLTNat.lt 0 D →
                  instLENat.le (Lax263307.ParameterResources.resource a K B n D)
                    (instHPow.hPow 2
                      (instHMul.hMul C
                        (instHPow.hPow (instHMul.hMul D (Lax263307.AlgorithmParameters.logarithm n)) d)))))

concepts.title: Collision and length bounds for independently sampled paths
concepts.description:
Let $Q$ be a random vertex set and let $q_v=\Pr[v\in Q]$. Two independent
samples intersect with probability at most $\sum_v q_v^2$. The probability
that an edge joins their vertex sets is at most the ordered adjacency mass
$\sum_{uv\in E(G)}2q_uq_v$. Also $\mathbb E[|Q|]=\sum_vq_v$.

Consequently, if $q_v\le\ell x_v/k$, $0\le x_v\le1$, $\sum_vx_v\le k$ with $k>0$,
and $e_G(x)\le k^2/p$ with $p>0$, these bounds are respectively
$\ell^2/k$, $2\ell^2/p$, and $\ell$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
A finite distribution is given explicitly by its outcome probabilities.
The pair probabilities are products, expressing independent sampling.
The estimates depend only on the vertex sets of the sampled paths, so the
definitions allow arbitrary finite vertex sets.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax263307.Entropy
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Card

/-!
---
title: Collision and length bounds for independently sampled paths
type: lemma
---
Let $Q$ be a random vertex set and let $q_v=\Pr[v\in Q]$. Two independent
samples intersect with probability at most $\sum_v q_v^2$. The probability
that an edge joins their vertex sets is at most the ordered adjacency mass
$\sum_{uv\in E(G)}2q_uq_v$. Also $\mathbb E[|Q|]=\sum_vq_v$.

Consequently, if $q_v\le\ell x_v/k$, $0\le x_v\le1$, $\sum_vx_v\le k$ with $k>0$,
and $e_G(x)\le k^2/p$ with $p>0$, these bounds are respectively
$\ell^2/k$, $2\ell^2/p$, and $\ell$.

# Formalization notes

A finite distribution is given explicitly by its outcome probabilities.
The pair probabilities are products, expressing independent sampling.
The estimates depend only on the vertex sets of the sampled paths, so the
definitions allow arbitrary finite vertex sets.
-/

namespace Lax263307.PathSampling

open Entropy (adjacencyMass edgeCost)
/-- Finite outcome probabilities and their associated vertex sets. -/
structure Distribution (n q : ℕ) where
  /-- Probability of each outcome. -/
  probability : Fin q → ℝ
  /-- Probabilities are nonnegative. -/
  nonnegative : ∀ i, 0 ≤ probability i
  /-- Total probability is one. -/
  normalized : (∑ i, probability i) = 1
  /-- The vertices used by each outcome. -/
  vertices : Fin q → Finset (Fin n)

/-- Probability of using a particular vertex. -/
noncomputable def load {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) (v : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, if v ∈ P.vertices i then P.probability i else 0

/-- Expected number of used vertices. -/
noncomputable def expectedSize {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, P.probability i * ((P.vertices i).card : ℝ)

/-- Probability that independent outcomes have a common vertex. -/
noncomputable def collisionProbability {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, ∑ j, if ¬Disjoint (P.vertices i) (P.vertices j) then
    P.probability i * P.probability j else 0

/-- Probability that a graph edge joins independent outcomes. -/
noncomputable def adjacencyProbability {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Distribution n q) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, ∑ j, if ∃ u ∈ P.vertices i, ∃ v ∈ P.vertices j, G.Adj u v then
    P.probability i * P.probability j else 0

/-- Sum of vertex-use probabilities equals expected size. -/
axiom expected_size_identity {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) :
  expectedSize P = ∑ v, load P v

/-- The union bound for intersection of two independent samples. -/
axiom collision_union_bound {n q : ℕ} (P : Distribution n q) :
  collisionProbability P ≤ ∑ v, (load P v) ^ 2

/-- The union bound for edges joining two independent samples. -/
axiom adjacency_union_bound {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Distribution n q) :
  adjacencyProbability G P ≤ adjacencyMass G (load P)

/-- The load hypotheses imply the three estimates used in sampling. -/
axiom sampling_bounds {n q : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (P : Distribution n q) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (k ℓ p : ℝ)
    (k_positive : 0 < k) (ℓ_nonnegative : 0 ≤ ℓ) (p_positive : 0 < p)
    (cost_bounds : ∀ v, 0 ≤ x v ∧ x v ≤ 1) (mass : (∑ v, x v) ≤ k)
    (load_bound : ∀ v, load P v ≤ ℓ * x v / k)
    (edge_bound : edgeCost G x ≤ k ^ 2 / p) :
    collisionProbability P ≤ ℓ ^ 2 / k ∧
      adjacencyProbability G P ≤ 2 * ℓ ^ 2 / p ∧ expectedSize P ≤ ℓ

end Lax263307.PathSampling

  Real.instLT.lt 0 k →
    Real.instLE.le 0 ℓ →
      Real.instLT.lt 0 p →
        (∀ (v : Fin n), And (Real.instLE.le 0 (x v)) (Real.instLE.le (x v) 1)) →
          Real.instLE.le (Finset.univ.sum fun v => x v) k →
